Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 46, verses 1–6:

Tafsir of Surah al-Ahqaf

It is a Meccan surah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

He, exalted is He, informs that He sent down the Book upon His servant and messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him always until the Day of Judgment. He described Himself with might that cannot be overcome, and with wisdom in His words and deeds. Then He said: ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾, meaning, not in vain or falsehood, ﴿and for a specified term﴾, meaning, until a fixed appointed period that neither increases nor decreases.

His saying: ﴿But those who disbelieve turn away from what they are warned﴾, meaning, they are heedless of what is intended for them, although a Book has been sent down to them and a messenger has been sent to them, and they turn away from all of that. That is, they will come to know its outcome.

Then He said: ﴿Say﴾, meaning, to these polytheists who worship other than Allah alongside Him: ﴿Have you considered those you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created from the earth﴾, meaning, show me the place where they have independently created anything from the earth. ﴿Or do they have a partnership in the heavens?﴾, meaning, they have no partnership in the heavens or on the earth, and they do not own even a speck (qitmir). Indeed, sovereignty and disposal belong entirely to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So how can you worship others alongside Him and associate partners with Him? Who guided you to this? Who called you to it? Did He command you to it, or is it something you have invented from yourselves? Therefore He said: ﴿Bring me a Book before this﴾, meaning, bring a Book from the Books of Allah revealed to the prophets, peace be upon them, that commands you to worship these idols. ﴿Or a trace of knowledge﴾, meaning, a clear proof for this path you have taken. ﴿If you are truthful﴾, meaning, you have no proof, neither transmitted nor rational, for that.

Therefore others recited: "or an athara (trace) of knowledge", meaning, knowledge that is sound and transmitted from someone before them, as Mujahid said regarding His saying: ﴿or a trace of knowledge﴾: "or someone transmitting knowledge."

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "or clear evidence from the matter."

Imam Ahmad narrated: Yahya related to us from Sufyan, Safwan ibn Sulaym related to us from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said. Sufyan said: I know of it only from the Prophet (ﷺ): "or a trace of knowledge" – he said: "the line (khatt)." [Al-Musnad (1/226).]

Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash said: "or a remnant of knowledge." Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿or a trace﴾ is something one extracts and stirs up.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash also said: ﴿or a trace of knowledge﴾ means the line (khatt).

Qatada said: ﴿or a trace of knowledge﴾ means special knowledge.

All these statements are close in meaning and return to what we have stated. This is the choice of Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, honor him, and grant him a good abode.

* *

His saying: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, one who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, while they are unaware of their supplication?﴾ meaning, none is more astray than one who calls upon idols and asks of them what they cannot do, until the Day of Resurrection, while they are heedless of what he says. They do not hear, do not see, and do not seize, because they are inanimate stones, deaf.

* *

His saying: ﴿And when people are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they have taken besides Allah gods that they might be for them a source of might. No! They will deny their worship of them and will be opposed to them﴾ [Maryam: 81–82], meaning, they will disown them at the time they most need them. And Khalil (Abraham) said: ﴿You have taken only idols besides Allah as a bond of affection among you in the worldly life; then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disbelieve in others and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 25].

Allah, exalted is He, says, reporting about the polytheists in their disbelief and obstinacy: when Allah's clear signs are recited to them, that is, while they are being explained, made plain and made manifest, they say: ﴿This is manifest magic﴾, that is, clear magic. They have lied, fabricated, gone astray and disbelieved. ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ meaning Muhammad ﷺ. Allah said: ﴿Say: If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me anything against Allah﴾, that is, if I had lied against Him and claimed that He had sent me, which is not the case, He would punish me with the severest punishment, and none of the people of the earth, neither you nor anyone else, could protect me from Him. This is like His saying: ﴿Say: Indeed, no one will protect me from Allah, nor will I find any refuge other than Him, except a notification from Allah and His messages﴾ [al-Jinn: 22-23]. And He said: ﴿And if he had attributed to Us some sayings. We would have seized him by the right hand. Then We would have cut from him the aorta. And none of you could prevent Us from him﴾ [al-Haqqah: 44-47]. Therefore He said here: ﴿Say: If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me anything against Allah. He is most knowing of what you say concerning it. Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you﴾. This is a threat to them, a firm warning and a severe intimidation.

* *

His saying: ﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ is an encouragement for them to repent and turn back, that is: despite all of this, if you return and repent, He will accept your repentance, pardon you, forgive you and show you mercy. This verse is like His saying in Surah al-Furqan: ﴿And they say, "Legends of the former peoples which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening." Say: "It has been sent down by He who knows the secret within the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful"﴾ [al-Furqan: 5-6].

* *

His saying: ﴿Say: I am not an innovation among the messengers﴾ means: I am not the first messenger to come to the world. Rather, messengers came before me, so I am not a matter without precedent that you should deny and find it strange that I have been sent to you, for Allah has indeed sent all the prophets before me to the nations.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said: ﴿Say: I am not an innovation among the messengers﴾ means: I am not the first messenger. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim did not report anything other than this.

* *

His saying: ﴿And I do not know what will be done with me or with you﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this verse: it was followed by ﴿That Allah may forgive you your sins, past and future﴾ [al-Fath: 2]. Likewise 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: it was abrogated by His saying: ﴿That Allah may forgive you your sins, past and future﴾. They said: When this verse was revealed, a man among the Muslims said: "Allah has made clear what He will do with you, O Messenger of Allah; so what will He do with us?" When Allah mentioned in the first verse the affirmation of His oneness, sincerity in worship, and steadfastness toward Him, He followed it with the command concerning parents, as it is linked in more than one verse of the Qur'an, such as His saying: ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you be good to parents﴾ [al-Isra: 23], and His saying: ﴿Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the final destination﴾ [Luqman: 14], and many other verses. Here He said: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾, meaning: We commanded him to be kind to them and to be tender toward them.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu'bah narrated to us, Simak ibn Harb informed me, who said: I heard Mus'ab ibn Sa'd narrate from Sa'd, who said: Sa'd's mother said to him: "Has not Allah commanded obedience to parents? I will not eat food or drink any drink until you disbelieve in Allah." She refused food and drink until they opened her mouth with a stick. Then this verse was revealed: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾ [al-Ankabut: 8] to the end of the verse.

Muslim and the authors of the Sunan (except Ibn Majah) related it from the hadith of Shu'bah with its chain, similarly and more extensively. [Musnad al-Tayalisi no. (208), Sahih Muslim no. (1748), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2740), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3079), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11196), but al-Nasa'i did not narrate the witness here, only its beginning.]

﴿His mother bore him with hardship﴾, meaning: she endured, because of him during his pregnancy, difficulty and fatigue, including nausea, faintness, heaviness, and distress, and other hardships that pregnant women suffer. ﴿And she gave birth to him with hardship﴾, meaning: with difficulty also, from the pangs of labour and their severity. ﴿And his bearing and weaning take thirty months﴾.

Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, used this verse together with the one in Luqman: ﴿And his weaning is in two years﴾ [Luqman: 14], and His saying: ﴿Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 233], to establish that the minimum period of pregnancy is six months. This is a strong and sound deduction. Uthman and a group of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, agreed with him.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said, from Yazid ibn Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Ba'jah ibn Abd Allah al-Juhani, who said: A man from among us married a woman from Juhaynah, and she gave birth to him after exactly six months. Her husband went to Uthman and told him of that, so he sent for her. When she rose to put on her clothes, her sister wept. She said: "What makes you weep? By Allah, no one among Allah's creation has ever touched me except him, so let Allah decide concerning me what He wills." When she was brought to Uthman, he ordered her stoned. This reached Ali, so he came to him and said: "What are you doing?" He said: "She gave birth to a full child after six months, and can that happen?" Ali said to him: "Do you not recite the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Have you not heard Allah say: ﴿And his bearing and weaning take thirty months﴾, and He says: ﴿Mothers [breastfeed their children] for two complete years﴾? So we find that only six months remain." He said: Uthman said: "By Allah, I did not perceive this. Bring me the woman." They found that she had already been dealt with. He said: Ba'jah said: "By Allah, no crow is more like a crow, and no egg more like an egg, than he is like his father." When his father saw him he said: "My son, by Allah, I have no doubt about him." He said: "And Allah afflicted him with this ulcer, the ulcer of the cancer [al-Ukalah], and it kept eating him until he died."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. We have cited it by another route at His saying: ﴿So I am the first of those who worship﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 81].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Farwah ibn Abi al-Maghra' narrated to us, Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: If a woman gives birth after nine months, the breastfeeding due to him is twenty-one months; if she gives birth to him after seven months, the breastfeeding due to him is twenty-three months; and if she gives birth to him after six months, then two complete years, because Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And his bearing and weaning take thirty months﴾.

﴿Until, when he reaches his maturity﴾, meaning: he becomes strong, grows up, and becomes a man, ﴿and reaches forty years﴾, meaning: his intellect reaches its full extent, and his understanding and forbearance become complete. It is said that generally he does not change from the state of a man of forty.

Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash said, from al-A'mash, from al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: I said to Masruq: "When is a man held accountable for his sins?" He said: "When you reach forty, then take your precaution."

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Ubayd Allah al-Qawariri narrated to us, Azrah ibn Qays al-Azdi narrated to us, and he had reached one hundred years old, Abu al-Hasan al-Salouli narrated to us, from him [and he added to me], who said: Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Uthman said, from Uthman, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "When a Muslim servant reaches forty years, Allah lightens his reckoning; when he reaches sixty years, Allah grants him repentance towards Him; when he reaches seventy years, the people of heaven love him; when he reaches eighty years, Allah makes his good deeds firm and erases his evil deeds; when he reaches ninety years, Allah forgives him what preceded of his sin and what followed, intercedes for him concerning his family, and it is written in heaven: 'The prisoner of Allah on His earth.'" [Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/205): "Abu Ya'la narrated it in al-Kabir, and in its chain is Azrah ibn Qays al-Azdi, who is weak."]

This has been narrated by another route, and it is in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad. [Imam Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, al-Musnad (3/218).]

Al-Hajjaj ibn Abd Allah al-Hakami, one of the commanders of the Banu Umayyah in Damascus, said: "I abandoned sins and wrongdoing for forty years out of shame before people, then I abandoned them out of shame before Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

How beautiful is the saying of the poet:

He pursued desire until grey hair overtook his head,
and when it overtook him he said to falsehood: "Be gone!"

﴿He said: My Lord, grant me inspiration﴾, meaning: inspire me ﴿to be grateful for Your favour which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteous deeds which You are pleased with﴾, meaning: in the future, ﴿and make my offspring righteous for me﴾, meaning: my descendants and my progeny, ﴿Indeed I have turned to You in repentance, and indeed I am among the Muslims﴾. This contains guidance for whoever reaches forty to renew repentance and turning back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and to resolve upon it.

Abu Dawud related in his Sunan, from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach them to say in the tashahhud: "O Allah, join our hearts together, reconcile our affairs, guide us to the paths of peace, bring us out of darknesses into light, keep us away from indecencies, whether apparent or hidden, bless us in our hearing, our sight, our hearts, our spouses, and our offspring, accept our repentance, for You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful, and make us grateful for Your favour, praising You for it, accepting it, and complete it upon us." [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (969).]

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds﴾, meaning: these are those characterized by what we have mentioned, those who repent to Allah and turn to Him, who make up through repentance and seeking forgiveness what they missed. They are the ones from whom the best of their deeds is accepted, and whose misdeeds are overlooked. He forgives them much of their slips and accepts from them the little of deeds. ﴿Among the companions of Paradise﴾, meaning: they are among the general body of the companions of Paradise, and this is their ruling with Allah, as Allah promised whoever repents to Him and turns back. Therefore He said: ﴿A true promise which they were promised﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from al-Ghutrif, from Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from the Trustworthy Spirit (Jibril), peace be upon him, who said: "The good deeds and evil deeds of the servant are brought, and some of them are settled against others. If a good deed remains, Allah expands for him in Paradise." He said: I entered upon Yazdad and he was told a similar hadith. He said: I said: "What if the good deed is gone?" He said: ﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds among the companions of Paradise, a true promise which they were promised﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari (26/12). Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah (3/91) from the route of Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman with it, and Abu Nu'aym said: "This is a strange hadith from the hadith of Jabir; al-Ghutrif is one whom al-Hakam ibn Aban al-Adani alone narrated from."]

Similarly, Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la al-San'ani, from Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, with its chain, similarly, and he added "from the Trustworthy Spirit," who said: "The Lord, Majestic is His majesty, said: 'The good deeds and evil deeds of the servant are brought...'" and he mentioned it. It is a strange hadith, with a good chain that is not objectionable.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Ma'bad narrated to us, Amr ibn Asim al-Kilabi narrated to us, Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr Ja'far ibn Abi Wahshiyah, from Yusuf ibn Sa'd [and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain], from Muhammad ibn Hatib, who said: When Ali prevailed over the people of Basrah, he stayed in my house. One day he said to me: "I was present with the Commander of the Faithful Ali, and with him were Ammar, Sa'sa'ah, al-Ashtar, and Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr. They mentioned Uthman and spoke ill of him. Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, was on the couch, with a stick in his hand. One of them said: 'Among you is someone who can decide between you,' so they asked him. Ali said: 'Uthman was among those whom Allah described: ﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds among the companions of Paradise, a true promise which they were promised﴾.'" He said: "By Allah, Uthman and the companions of Uthman," saying it three times. Yusuf said: I said to Muhammad ibn Hatib: "By Allah, did you hear this from Ali?" He said: "By Allah, I heard this from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him."

When Allah mentioned in the first verse the affirmation of His oneness, sincerity in worship, and steadfastness toward Him, He followed it with the command concerning parents, as it is linked in more than one verse of the Qur'an, such as His saying: ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you be good to parents﴾ [al-Isra: 23], and His saying: ﴿Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the final destination﴾ [Luqman: 14], and many other verses. Here He said: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾, meaning: We commanded him to be kind to them and to be tender toward them.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu'bah narrated to us, Simak ibn Harb informed me, who said: I heard Mus'ab ibn Sa'd narrate from Sa'd, who said: Sa'd's mother said to him: "Has not Allah commanded obedience to parents? I will not eat food or drink any drink until you disbelieve in Allah." She refused food and drink until they opened her mouth with a stick. Then this verse was revealed: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾ [al-Ankabut: 8] to the end of the verse.

Muslim and the authors of the Sunan (except Ibn Majah) related it from the hadith of Shu'bah with its chain, similarly and more extensively. [Musnad al-Tayalisi no. (208), Sahih Muslim no. (1748), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2740), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3079), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11196), but al-Nasa'i did not narrate the witness here, only its beginning.]

﴿His mother bore him with hardship﴾, meaning: she endured, because of him during his pregnancy, difficulty and fatigue, including nausea, faintness, heaviness, and distress, and other hardships that pregnant women suffer. ﴿And she gave birth to him with hardship﴾, meaning: with difficulty also, from the pangs of labour and their severity. ﴿And his bearing and weaning take thirty months﴾.

Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, used this verse together with the one in Luqman: ﴿And his weaning is in two years﴾ [Luqman: 14], and His saying: ﴿Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 233], to establish that the minimum period of pregnancy is six months. This is a strong and sound deduction. Uthman and a group of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, agreed with him.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said, from Yazid ibn Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Ba'jah ibn Abd Allah al-Juhani, who said: A man from among us married a woman from Juhaynah, and she gave birth to him after exactly six months. Her husband went to Uthman and told him of that, so he sent for her. When she rose to put on her clothes, her sister wept. She said: "What makes you weep? By Allah, no one among Allah's creation has ever touched me except him, so let Allah decide concerning me what He wills." When she was brought to Uthman, he ordered her stoned. This reached Ali, so he came to him and said: "What are you doing?" He said: "She gave birth to a full child after six months, and can that happen?" Ali said to him: "Do you not recite the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Have you not heard Allah say: ﴿And his bearing and weaning take thirty months﴾, and He says: ﴿Mothers [breastfeed their children] for two complete years﴾? So we find that only six months remain." He said: Uthman said: "By Allah, I did not perceive this. Bring me the woman." They found that she had already been dealt with. He said: Ba'jah said: "By Allah, no crow is more like a crow, and no egg more like an egg, than he is like his father." When his father saw him he said: "My son, by Allah, I have no doubt about him." He said: "And Allah afflicted him with this ulcer, the ulcer of the cancer [al-Ukalah], and it kept eating him until he died."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. We have cited it by another route at His saying: ﴿So I am the first of those who worship﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 81].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Farwah ibn Abi al-Maghra' narrated to us, Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: If a woman gives birth after nine months, the breastfeeding due to him is twenty-one months; if she gives birth to him after seven months, the breastfeeding due to him is twenty-three months; and if she gives birth to him after six months, then two complete years, because Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And his bearing and weaning take thirty months﴾.

﴿Until, when he reaches his maturity﴾, meaning: he becomes strong, grows up, and becomes a man, ﴿and reaches forty years﴾, meaning: his intellect reaches its full extent, and his understanding and forbearance become complete. It is said that generally he does not change from the state of a man of forty.

Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash said, from al-A'mash, from al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: I said to Masruq: "When is a man held accountable for his sins?" He said: "When you reach forty, then take your precaution."

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Ubayd Allah al-Qawariri narrated to us, Azrah ibn Qays al-Azdi narrated to us, and he had reached one hundred years old, Abu al-Hasan al-Salouli narrated to us, from him [and he added to me], who said: Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Uthman said, from Uthman, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "When a Muslim servant reaches forty years, Allah lightens his reckoning; when he reaches sixty years, Allah grants him repentance towards Him; when he reaches seventy years, the people of heaven love him; when he reaches eighty years, Allah makes his good deeds firm and erases his evil deeds; when he reaches ninety years, Allah forgives him what preceded of his sin and what followed, intercedes for him concerning his family, and it is written in heaven: 'The prisoner of Allah on His earth.'" [Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/205): "Abu Ya'la narrated it in al-Kabir, and in its chain is Azrah ibn Qays al-Azdi, who is weak."]

This has been narrated by another route, and it is in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad. [Imam Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, al-Musnad (3/218).]

Al-Hajjaj ibn Abd Allah al-Hakami, one of the commanders of the Banu Umayyah in Damascus, said: "I abandoned sins and wrongdoing for forty years out of shame before people, then I abandoned them out of shame before Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

How beautiful is the saying of the poet:

He pursued desire until grey hair overtook his head,
and when it overtook him he said to falsehood: "Be gone!"

﴿He said: My Lord, grant me inspiration﴾, meaning: inspire me ﴿to be grateful for Your favour which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteous deeds which You are pleased with﴾, meaning: in the future, ﴿and make my offspring righteous for me﴾, meaning: my descendants and my progeny, ﴿Indeed I have turned to You in repentance, and indeed I am among the Muslims﴾. This contains guidance for whoever reaches forty to renew repentance and turning back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and to resolve upon it.

Abu Dawud related in his Sunan, from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach them to say in the tashahhud: "O Allah, join our hearts together, reconcile our affairs, guide us to the paths of peace, bring us out of darknesses into light, keep us away from indecencies, whether apparent or hidden, bless us in our hearing, our sight, our hearts, our spouses, and our offspring, accept our repentance, for You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful, and make us grateful for Your favour, praising You for it, accepting it, and complete it upon us." [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (969).]

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds﴾, meaning: these are those characterized by what we have mentioned, those who repent to Allah and turn to Him, who make up through repentance and seeking forgiveness what they missed. They are the ones from whom the best of their deeds is accepted, and whose misdeeds are overlooked. He forgives them much of their slips and accepts from them the little of deeds. ﴿Among the companions of Paradise﴾, meaning: they are among the general body of the companions of Paradise, and this is their ruling with Allah, as Allah promised whoever repents to Him and turns back. Therefore He said: ﴿A true promise which they were promised﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from al-Ghutrif, from Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from the Trustworthy Spirit (Jibril), peace be upon him, who said: "The good deeds and evil deeds of the servant are brought, and some of them are settled against others. If a good deed remains, Allah expands for him in Paradise." He said: I entered upon Yazdad and he was told a similar hadith. He said: I said: "What if the good deed is gone?" He said: ﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds among the companions of Paradise, a true promise which they were promised﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari (26/12). Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah (3/91) from the route of Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman with it, and Abu Nu'aym said: "This is a strange hadith from the hadith of Jabir; al-Ghutrif is one whom al-Hakam ibn Aban al-Adani alone narrated from."]

Similarly, Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la al-San'ani, from Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, with its chain, similarly, and he added "from the Trustworthy Spirit," who said: "The Lord, Majestic is His majesty, said: 'The good deeds and evil deeds of the servant are brought...'" and he mentioned it. It is a strange hadith, with a good chain that is not objectionable.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Ma'bad narrated to us, Amr ibn Asim al-Kilabi narrated to us, Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr Ja'far ibn Abi Wahshiyah, from Yusuf ibn Sa'd [and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain], from Muhammad ibn Hatib, who said: When Ali prevailed over the people of Basrah, he stayed in my house. One day he said to me: "I was present with the Commander of the Faithful Ali, and with him were Ammar, Sa'sa'ah, al-Ashtar, and Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr. They mentioned Uthman and spoke ill of him. Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, was on the couch, with a stick in his hand. One of them said: 'Among you is someone who can decide between you,' so they asked him. Ali said: 'Uthman was among those whom Allah described: ﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds among the companions of Paradise, a true promise which they were promised﴾.'" He said: "By Allah, Uthman and the companions of Uthman," saying it three times. Yusuf said: I said to Muhammad ibn Hatib: "By Allah, did you hear this from Ali?" He said: "By Allah, I heard this from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 46, verse 17–20:

When Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the state of those who supplicate for their dutiful parents and what they will attain with Him of success and salvation, He followed it with the state of the wretched who disobey their parents, saying: ﴿And he who says to his parents, "Uff to you both!"﴾ This applies generally to everyone who says this. As for the one who claims that it was revealed concerning ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, his claim is weak, because ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr embraced Islam afterwards, his Islam was good, and he was among the best people of his time.

Al-ʿAwfi narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that it was revealed concerning a son of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. There is scrutiny regarding the soundness of this, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Jurayj said, from Mujahid: it was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Bakr. Ibn Jurayj also said this.

Others said: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr. This was also said by al-Suddi. Rather, this is general to everyone who disobeys his parents and denies the truth; when he says to his parents, "Uff to you both!", he has disobeyed them.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: ʿAli ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-ʿAla narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Zaidah narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Madini informed me, saying: I was in the mosque when Marwan gave a sermon, and he said: Indeed Allah has shown the Commander of the Faithful a good opinion regarding Yazid, and if he appoints him as successor, then Abu Bakr had appointed ʿUmar as successor. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr said: Heraclian (Hiraqliyyah)?! By Allah, Abu Bakr did not place it (the caliphate) in any of his sons, nor in anyone of his family, and Muʿawiyah did not place it in his son except out of mercy and honour for his son. Marwan said: Are you not the one who said to his parents, "Uff to you both!"? ʿAbd al-Rahman said: Are you not the son of the accursed one whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed, your father? He said: ʿAʾishah heard them both and said: O Marwan, are you the one who says such and such to ʿAbd al-Rahman? You have lied; it was not revealed concerning him, but it was revealed concerning so-and-so son of so-and-so. Then Marwan wept, then he descended from the pulpit until he came to the door of her chamber, and he began speaking to her until he departed.

This has also been narrated by al-Bukhari with a different chain and wording. He said: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Abu ʿAwanah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Yusuf ibn Mahak, who said: Marwan was over the Hijaz, appointed by Muʿawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan. He gave a sermon and began mentioning Yazid ibn Muʿawiyah so that allegiance would be pledged to him after his father. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr said something to him, so he said: Seize him. He entered the house of ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and they could not reach him. Marwan said: Indeed, this is the one concerning whom this was revealed: ﴿And he who says to his parents, "Uff to you both! Do you promise me that I will be brought forth when generations have passed before me?"﴾ ʿAʾishah said from behind the curtain: Allah did not reveal anything of the Qur'an concerning us, except that Allah revealed my innocence.

Another route: al-Nasa'i said: ʿAli ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Umayyah ibn Khalid narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, who said: When Muʿawiyah pledged allegiance for his son, Marwan said: The sunnah of Abu Bakr and ʿUmar. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr said: The sunnah of Heraclius and Caesar. Marwan said: This is the one concerning whom Allah revealed: ﴿And he who says to his parents, "Uff to you both"﴾ and so on. This reached ʿAʾishah, and she said: Marwan has lied! By Allah, it is not about him. If I wished to name the one concerning whom it was revealed, I would name him, but the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the father of Marwan, and Marwan was in his loins, so Marwan is a portion of the curse of Allah.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Do you promise me that I will be brought forth?﴾, meaning: that I will be resurrected, ﴿when generations have passed before me?﴾, meaning: that people have passed away and no one has returned from them to inform. ﴿While they both seek Allah's help﴾, meaning: they ask Allah concerning him to guide him, and they say to their son: ﴿Woe to you! Believe, for the promise of Allah is true.﴾ But he says: ﴿This is nothing but the fables of the ancients.﴾ Allah said: ﴿Those are they against whom the word has come into effect among nations that had passed away before them of jinn and men. Indeed, they were losers.﴾ That is, they entered into the company of their likes and kind of the disbelieving losers, who lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

His saying: ﴿Those﴾ after ﴿And he who says﴾ is evidence for what we have mentioned, that it is a category encompassing everyone who is like that.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: he is the disbelieving, wicked one who disobeys his parents, who denies the Resurrection.

Al-Hafiz Ibn ʿAsakir narrated in the biography of Sahl ibn Dawud, by way of Hisham ibn ʿAmmar: Hammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, Khalid ibn al-Zibriqan al-Halabi narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Habib al-Muharibi, from Abu Umamah al-Bahili, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Four whom Allah has cursed from above His Throne, and the angels have said Amen to their curse: the one who misleads the needy (Khalid said: the one who reaches his hand out to the poor man and says, 'Come, I will give you,' and when he comes, he says, 'I have nothing with me'), the one who tells the blind man, 'Beware of the animal,' while there is nothing before him, the man who is asked about the house of a people and directs him to other than it, and the one who beats his parents until they cry out for help." Very strange indeed.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And for each are degrees according to what they did﴾, meaning: for each there is a punishment according to his deeds, ﴿and that He may fulfil for them their deeds, and they will not be wronged﴾, meaning: He will not wrong them the weight of an atom or less than that.

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: The degrees of the Fire go downward, and the degrees of Paradise go upward.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the Day when those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire: "You squandered your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them"﴾, meaning: this will be said to them as rebuke and reproach. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, used to abstain from many good foods and drinks and kept himself away from them, and he would say: I fear that I may be like those to whom Allah, the Exalted, said, rebuking them: ﴿You squandered your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them.﴾

Abu Mijlaz said: Groups of people will certainly be reckoned for the good deeds they had in the world, and it will be said to them: ﴿You squandered your good things in your worldly life.﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you were arrogant about in the earth without right and for what you used to defiantly disobey﴾, they will be repaid in kind with their deeds. Just as they indulged themselves and were arrogant toward following the truth, and engaged in sin and disobedience, Allah requited them with the punishment of humiliation, which is disgrace, shame, painful torment, successive regrets, and dwelling in the terrifying levels of the Fire. May Allah protect us from all of that.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 46, verse 17–20:

When Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the state of those who supplicate for their dutiful parents and what they will attain with Him of success and salvation, He followed it with the state of the wretched who disobey their parents, saying: ﴿And he who says to his parents, "Uff to you both!"﴾ This applies generally to everyone who says this. As for the one who claims that it was revealed concerning ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, his claim is weak, because ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr embraced Islam afterwards, his Islam was good, and he was among the best people of his time.

Al-ʿAwfi narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that it was revealed concerning a son of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. There is scrutiny regarding the soundness of this, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Jurayj said, from Mujahid: it was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Bakr. Ibn Jurayj also said this.

Others said: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr. This was also said by al-Suddi. Rather, this is general to everyone who disobeys his parents and denies the truth; when he says to his parents, "Uff to you both!", he has disobeyed them.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: ʿAli ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-ʿAla narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Zaidah narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Madini informed me, saying: I was in the mosque when Marwan gave a sermon, and he said: Indeed Allah has shown the Commander of the Faithful a good opinion regarding Yazid, and if he appoints him as successor, then Abu Bakr had appointed ʿUmar as successor. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr said: Heraclian (Hiraqliyyah)?! By Allah, Abu Bakr did not place it (the caliphate) in any of his sons, nor in anyone of his family, and Muʿawiyah did not place it in his son except out of mercy and honour for his son. Marwan said: Are you not the one who said to his parents, "Uff to you both!"? ʿAbd al-Rahman said: Are you not the son of the accursed one whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed, your father? He said: ʿAʾishah heard them both and said: O Marwan, are you the one who says such and such to ʿAbd al-Rahman? You have lied; it was not revealed concerning him, but it was revealed concerning so-and-so son of so-and-so. Then Marwan wept, then he descended from the pulpit until he came to the door of her chamber, and he began speaking to her until he departed.

This has also been narrated by al-Bukhari with a different chain and wording. He said: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Abu ʿAwanah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Yusuf ibn Mahak, who said: Marwan was over the Hijaz, appointed by Muʿawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan. He gave a sermon and began mentioning Yazid ibn Muʿawiyah so that allegiance would be pledged to him after his father. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr said something to him, so he said: Seize him. He entered the house of ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and they could not reach him. Marwan said: Indeed, this is the one concerning whom this was revealed: ﴿And he who says to his parents, "Uff to you both! Do you promise me that I will be brought forth when generations have passed before me?"﴾ ʿAʾishah said from behind the curtain: Allah did not reveal anything of the Qur'an concerning us, except that Allah revealed my innocence.

Another route: al-Nasa'i said: ʿAli ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Umayyah ibn Khalid narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, who said: When Muʿawiyah pledged allegiance for his son, Marwan said: The sunnah of Abu Bakr and ʿUmar. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr said: The sunnah of Heraclius and Caesar. Marwan said: This is the one concerning whom Allah revealed: ﴿And he who says to his parents, "Uff to you both"﴾ and so on. This reached ʿAʾishah, and she said: Marwan has lied! By Allah, it is not about him. If I wished to name the one concerning whom it was revealed, I would name him, but the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the father of Marwan, and Marwan was in his loins, so Marwan is a portion of the curse of Allah.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Do you promise me that I will be brought forth?﴾, meaning: that I will be resurrected, ﴿when generations have passed before me?﴾, meaning: that people have passed away and no one has returned from them to inform. ﴿While they both seek Allah's help﴾, meaning: they ask Allah concerning him to guide him, and they say to their son: ﴿Woe to you! Believe, for the promise of Allah is true.﴾ But he says: ﴿This is nothing but the fables of the ancients.﴾ Allah said: ﴿Those are they against whom the word has come into effect among nations that had passed away before them of jinn and men. Indeed, they were losers.﴾ That is, they entered into the company of their likes and kind of the disbelieving losers, who lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

His saying: ﴿Those﴾ after ﴿And he who says﴾ is evidence for what we have mentioned, that it is a category encompassing everyone who is like that.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: he is the disbelieving, wicked one who disobeys his parents, who denies the Resurrection.

Al-Hafiz Ibn ʿAsakir narrated in the biography of Sahl ibn Dawud, by way of Hisham ibn ʿAmmar: Hammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, Khalid ibn al-Zibriqan al-Halabi narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Habib al-Muharibi, from Abu Umamah al-Bahili, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Four whom Allah has cursed from above His Throne, and the angels have said Amen to their curse: the one who misleads the needy (Khalid said: the one who reaches his hand out to the poor man and says, 'Come, I will give you,' and when he comes, he says, 'I have nothing with me'), the one who tells the blind man, 'Beware of the animal,' while there is nothing before him, the man who is asked about the house of a people and directs him to other than it, and the one who beats his parents until they cry out for help." Very strange indeed.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And for each are degrees according to what they did﴾, meaning: for each there is a punishment according to his deeds, ﴿and that He may fulfil for them their deeds, and they will not be wronged﴾, meaning: He will not wrong them the weight of an atom or less than that.

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: The degrees of the Fire go downward, and the degrees of Paradise go upward.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the Day when those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire: "You squandered your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them"﴾, meaning: this will be said to them as rebuke and reproach. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, used to abstain from many good foods and drinks and kept himself away from them, and he would say: I fear that I may be like those to whom Allah, the Exalted, said, rebuking them: ﴿You squandered your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them.﴾

Abu Mijlaz said: Groups of people will certainly be reckoned for the good deeds they had in the world, and it will be said to them: ﴿You squandered your good things in your worldly life.﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you were arrogant about in the earth without right and for what you used to defiantly disobey﴾, they will be repaid in kind with their deeds. Just as they indulged themselves and were arrogant toward following the truth, and engaged in sin and disobedience, Allah requited them with the punishment of humiliation, which is disgrace, shame, painful torment, successive regrets, and dwelling in the terrifying levels of the Fire. May Allah protect us from all of that.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 46, verses 21–25:

He, exalted is He, says, consoling His Prophet regarding the denial of those among his people who denied him: ﴿And mention the brother of 'Ad﴾, who was Hud, peace be upon him. God sent him to the first 'Ad, and they used to dwell in al-Ahqaf (the plural of *haqf*, which is a mountain of sand), as Ibn Zayd said. 'Ikrimah said: al-Ahqaf means a mountain and a cave. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: al-Ahqaf is a valley in Hadramawt called Burhut, where the spirits of the disbelievers are cast. Qatadah said: "It has been mentioned to us that 'Ad were a people in Yemen, people of sand overlooking the sea, in a land called al-Shihr."

Ibn Majah said: "Chapter: When one supplicates, let him begin with himself." Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Khallal narrated to us: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "May God have mercy on us and on the brother of 'Ad."[[Sunan Ibn Majah (3852). al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/204): "This is a sound chain, and it has corroborating reports in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b."]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And warners had come before him and after him﴾ means: God had sent messengers and warners to the towns surrounding their lands, like His saying: ﴿So We made it an example for what was before it and what was after it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 66], and like His saying: ﴿But if they turn away, say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud, when the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them, saying: Worship none but God. They said: If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels; so indeed we disbelieve in what you have been sent with﴾ [Fussilat: 13–14].[[In M: "tawallaw" (they turned away), which is an error.]][[In T, M, A, H: "Inni akhafu 'alaykum 'adhab yawm 'azim" (Indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day), and the correct reading is what we have adopted.]] That is, Hud said this to them, and his people answered him, saying: ﴿Have you come to us to turn us away﴾, that is, to divert us ﴿from our gods? Then bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful﴾.

They sought to hasten the punishment and retribution of God, considering its occurrence unlikely, like His saying: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it﴾ [al-Shura: 18].

﴿He said: Knowledge is only with God﴾, that is: God knows best about you. If you deserve the hastening of the punishment, He will do that to you.[[In M, A: "fasayaf'alu" (so He will do).]] As for me, it is my duty to convey to you what I have been sent with. ﴿But I see you as a people who are ignorant﴾, that is, you do not reason and do not understand.

God, exalted is He, says: ﴿So when they saw it as a cloud coming toward their valleys﴾, that is, when they saw the punishment approaching them, they supposed it was a rain-bearing cloud, so they rejoiced and were glad at it, though they had been in drought and in need of rain. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Rather, it is what you were hastening: a wind in which is a painful punishment﴾, that is, it is the punishment about which you said: ﴿Then bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful﴾.

﴿Destroying﴾, that is, ruining ﴿everything﴾ in their lands that is liable to ruin, ﴿by the command of its Lord﴾, that is, by God's permission to it in that, like His saying: ﴿It leaves nothing it comes upon but makes it like something crumbled to dust﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 42], that is, like something decayed. Hence He said: ﴿So they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings﴾, that is, they all perished to the last of them, and none of them remained. ﴿Thus We recompense the criminal people﴾, that is, this is Our judgment upon whoever denies Our messengers and opposes Our command.

A hadith has come concerning their story, and it is extremely strange, one of the strangest hadiths and of those narrated by a single transmitter. Imam Ahmad said:

Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to me; Abu al-Mundhir Sallam ibn Sulayman al-Nahwi narrated to me, saying: 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud narrated to us, from Abu Wa'il, from al-Harith al-Bakri, who said: I set out to complain about al-'Ala' ibn al-Hadrami to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). I passed by al-Rabadhah and found an old woman of Banu Tamim stranded there. She said to me: "O servant of God, I have a need with the Messenger of God (ﷺ); will you convey me to him?" So I carried her and brought her to Madinah. The mosque was packed with people, and a black banner was fluttering, and Bilal was wearing a sword before the Messenger of God (ﷺ). I said: "What is the matter with the people?" They said: "He intends to send 'Amr ibn al-'As on an expedition." So I sat down, and he entered his dwelling, or said: his lodging. I asked permission to see him, and he permitted me. I entered and greeted him, and he said: "Was there anything between you and Tamim?" I said: "Yes, and we had the upper hand over them. I passed by an old woman of Banu Tamim who was stranded, and she asked me to carry her to you, and here she is at the door." He permitted her, and she entered. I said: "O Messenger of God, if you see fit to make a barrier between us and Tamim, then make it al-Dahna'." The old woman grew angry and rose quickly and said: "O Messenger of God, then where will your distressed one (*mudtarr*) go?" He said: I said: "My example is that of what the first one said: 'A goat that carried its own death.' I carried this one without realizing she was an adversary to me. I seek refuge in God and His Messenger from being like the envoy of 'Ad." He said: "Go on, and what was the envoy of 'Ad?"—and he knew the story better than him, but he wanted him to recount it. I said: "'Ad suffered drought, so they sent an envoy named Qayl. He passed by Mu'awiyah ibn Bakr and stayed with him for a month, being given wine to drink while two slave-girls called 'al-Jaradatan' sang to him. When the month passed, he went out to the mountains of Mahrah and said: 'O God, You know that I have not come to a sick person to treat him, nor to a captive to ransom him. O God, give 'Ad to drink as You used to give them.' Then dark clouds passed by him, and he was called from among them: 'Choose.' He pointed to a black cloud among them, and he was called from it: 'Take it as ashes, scattering, leaving none of 'Ad alive.'" He said: "It was not reported to me that any wind was sent upon them except as much as flows through this ring of mine, until they perished." Abu Wa'il said: "And he spoke the truth." And when they sent an envoy among them, the man and the woman would say: "Do not be like the envoy of 'Ad."

Al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it, as has passed in surah al-A'raf.[[Al-Musnad (3/482); see the takhrij of the rest of this hadith under verse 73 of surah al-A'raf.]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us; Ibn Wahb informed us; 'Amr informed us, that Abu al-Nadr narrated to him, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from 'A'ishah[[In T: "'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her."]], that she said: "I never saw the Messenger of God (ﷺ) laughing so fully that I could see his uvula; he only smiled." She said: "And when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) saw a cloud or wind, it was recognized in his face." She said: "O Messenger of God, people rejoice when they see a cloud, hoping it will bring rain, but I see you, when you see it, recognize aversion in your face?" He said: "O 'A'ishah, what assures me that there is not in it a punishment? A people were punished by wind, and a people saw the punishment and said: 'This is a cloud bringing us rain.'" Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it from the narration of Ibn Wahb.[[Al-Musnad (6/66); Sahih al-Bukhari (4828, 4829); Sahih Muslim (899).]]

Another route: Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh, from his father, from 'A'ishah, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) whenever he saw a rising cloud on one of the horizons of the sky, would leave his work, even if he was in prayer, then say: "O God, I seek refuge in You from the evil that is in it."[[In M: "min su' 'aqibatihi" (from the evil of its consequence).]] If God removed it, he praised God, and if it rained he said: "O God, let it be a beneficial rain."[[Al-Musnad (6/190).]]

Another route: Muslim said in his Sahih: Abu al-Tahir narrated to us; Ibn Wahb informed us; I heard Ibn Jurayj narrating from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from 'A'ishah, who said: "When the wind blew strongly, the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) would say: 'O God, I ask You for its good, and the good of what is in it, and the good of what it was sent with, and I seek refuge in You from its evil, and the evil of what is in it, and the evil of what it was sent with.'" She said: "And when the sky became overcast, his colour changed, and he would go out and come in, and advance and withdraw. When it rained, he was relieved, and 'A'ishah recognized that, so she asked him, and he said: 'Perhaps, O 'A'ishah, it is as the people of 'Ad said: ﴿When they saw it as a cloud coming toward their valleys, they said: This is a cloud bringing us rain﴾."[[Sahih Muslim (899).]]

We have mentioned the story of the destruction of 'Ad in the two surahs al-A'raf and Hud, which is sufficient so that it need not be repeated here, and to God belongs praise and favour.

Al-Tabarani said: 'Abdan ibn Ahmad narrated to us; Isma'il ibn Zakariyya al-Kufi narrated to us; Abu Malik narrated to us, from Muslim al-Mula'i, from Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr,[[In T: "And al-Tabarani narrated with his chain."]] from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Only the size of a ring's opening of wind was released upon 'Ad. Then it was sent upon them, carrying them [from] the desert to the settled lands. When the people of the settled lands saw it, they said: 'This is a cloud bringing us rain, approaching our valleys.' The people of the desert were in it, so the people of the desert were thrown upon the people of the settled lands until they perished. He said: It rose over its keepers until it came out through the cracks of the doors."[[In T: "houses."]][[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/42). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/113): "In it is Muslim al-Mula'i, who is weak."]]

He said: "It was not reported to me that any wind was sent upon them except as much as flows through this ring of mine, until they perished." Abu Wa'il said: "And he spoke the truth." And when they sent an envoy among them, the man and the woman would say: "Do not be like the envoy of 'Ad."

Al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it, as has passed in surah al-A'raf.[[Al-Musnad (3/482); see the takhrij of the rest of this hadith under verse 73 of surah al-A'raf.]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us; Ibn Wahb informed us; 'Amr informed us, that Abu al-Nadr narrated to him, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from 'A'ishah[[In T: "'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her."]], that she said: "I never saw the Messenger of God (ﷺ) laughing so fully that I could see his uvula; he only smiled." She said: "And when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) saw a cloud or wind, it was recognized in his face." She said: "O Messenger of God, people rejoice when they see a cloud, hoping it will bring rain, but I see you, when you see it, recognize aversion in your face?" He said: "O 'A'ishah, what assures me that there is not in it a punishment? A people were punished by wind, and a people saw the punishment and said: 'This is a cloud bringing us rain.'" Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it from the narration of Ibn Wahb.[[Al-Musnad (6/66); Sahih al-Bukhari (4828, 4829); Sahih Muslim (899).]]

Another route: Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh, from his father, from 'A'ishah, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) whenever he saw a rising cloud on one of the horizons of the sky, would leave his work, even if he was in prayer, then say: "O God, I seek refuge in You from the evil that is in it."[[In M: "min su' 'aqibatihi" (from the evil of its consequence).]] If God removed it, he praised God, and if it rained he said: "O God, let it be a beneficial rain."[[Al-Musnad (6/190).]]

Another route: Muslim said in his Sahih: Abu al-Tahir narrated to us; Ibn Wahb informed us; I heard Ibn Jurayj narrating from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from 'A'ishah, who said: "When the wind blew strongly, the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) would say: 'O God, I ask You for its good, and the good of what is in it, and the good of what it was sent with, and I seek refuge in You from its evil, and the evil of what is in it, and the evil of what it was sent with.'" She said: "And when the sky became overcast, his colour changed, and he would go out and come in, and advance and withdraw. When it rained, he was relieved, and 'A'ishah recognized that, so she asked him, and he said: 'Perhaps, O 'A'ishah, it is as the people of 'Ad said: ﴿When they saw it as a cloud coming toward their valleys, they said: This is a cloud bringing us rain﴾."[[Sahih Muslim (899).]]

We have mentioned the story of the destruction of 'Ad in the two surahs al-A'raf and Hud, which is sufficient so that it need not be repeated here, and to God belongs praise and favour.

Al-Tabarani said: 'Abdan ibn Ahmad narrated to us; Isma'il ibn Zakariyya al-Kufi narrated to us; Abu Malik narrated to us, from Muslim al-Mula'i, from Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr,[[In T: "And al-Tabarani narrated with his chain."]] from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Only the size of a ring's opening of wind was released upon 'Ad. Then it was sent upon them, carrying them [from] the desert to the settled lands. When the people of the settled lands saw it, they said: 'This is a cloud bringing us rain, approaching our valleys.' The people of the desert were in it, so the people of the desert were thrown upon the people of the settled lands until they perished. He said: It rose over its keepers until it came out through the cracks of the doors."[[In T: "houses."]][[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/42). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/113): "In it is Muslim al-Mula'i, who is weak."]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 46, verses 21–25:

He, exalted is He, says, consoling His Prophet regarding the denial of those among his people who denied him: ﴿And mention the brother of 'Ad﴾, who was Hud, peace be upon him. God sent him to the first 'Ad, and they used to dwell in al-Ahqaf (the plural of *haqf*, which is a mountain of sand), as Ibn Zayd said. 'Ikrimah said: al-Ahqaf means a mountain and a cave. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: al-Ahqaf is a valley in Hadramawt called Burhut, where the spirits of the disbelievers are cast. Qatadah said: "It has been mentioned to us that 'Ad were a people in Yemen, people of sand overlooking the sea, in a land called al-Shihr."

Ibn Majah said: "Chapter: When one supplicates, let him begin with himself." Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Khallal narrated to us: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "May God have mercy on us and on the brother of 'Ad."[[Sunan Ibn Majah (3852). al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/204): "This is a sound chain, and it has corroborating reports in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b."]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And warners had come before him and after him﴾ means: God had sent messengers and warners to the towns surrounding their lands, like His saying: ﴿So We made it an example for what was before it and what was after it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 66], and like His saying: ﴿But if they turn away, say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud, when the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them, saying: Worship none but God. They said: If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels; so indeed we disbelieve in what you have been sent with﴾ [Fussilat: 13–14].[[In M: "tawallaw" (they turned away), which is an error.]][[In T, M, A, H: "Inni akhafu 'alaykum 'adhab yawm 'azim" (Indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day), and the correct reading is what we have adopted.]] That is, Hud said this to them, and his people answered him, saying: ﴿Have you come to us to turn us away﴾, that is, to divert us ﴿from our gods? Then bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful﴾.

They sought to hasten the punishment and retribution of God, considering its occurrence unlikely, like His saying: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it﴾ [al-Shura: 18].

﴿He said: Knowledge is only with God﴾, that is: God knows best about you. If you deserve the hastening of the punishment, He will do that to you.[[In M, A: "fasayaf'alu" (so He will do).]] As for me, it is my duty to convey to you what I have been sent with. ﴿But I see you as a people who are ignorant﴾, that is, you do not reason and do not understand.

God, exalted is He, says: ﴿So when they saw it as a cloud coming toward their valleys﴾, that is, when they saw the punishment approaching them, they supposed it was a rain-bearing cloud, so they rejoiced and were glad at it, though they had been in drought and in need of rain. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Rather, it is what you were hastening: a wind in which is a painful punishment﴾, that is, it is the punishment about which you said: ﴿Then bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful﴾.

﴿Destroying﴾, that is, ruining ﴿everything﴾ in their lands that is liable to ruin, ﴿by the command of its Lord﴾, that is, by God's permission to it in that, like His saying: ﴿It leaves nothing it comes upon but makes it like something crumbled to dust﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 42], that is, like something decayed. Hence He said: ﴿So they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings﴾, that is, they all perished to the last of them, and none of them remained. ﴿Thus We recompense the criminal people﴾, that is, this is Our judgment upon whoever denies Our messengers and opposes Our command.

A hadith has come concerning their story, and it is extremely strange, one of the strangest hadiths and of those narrated by a single transmitter. Imam Ahmad said:

Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to me; Abu al-Mundhir Sallam ibn Sulayman al-Nahwi narrated to me, saying: 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud narrated to us, from Abu Wa'il, from al-Harith al-Bakri, who said: I set out to complain about al-'Ala' ibn al-Hadrami to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). I passed by al-Rabadhah and found an old woman of Banu Tamim stranded there. She said to me: "O servant of God, I have a need with the Messenger of God (ﷺ); will you convey me to him?" So I carried her and brought her to Madinah. The mosque was packed with people, and a black banner was fluttering, and Bilal was wearing a sword before the Messenger of God (ﷺ). I said: "What is the matter with the people?" They said: "He intends to send 'Amr ibn al-'As on an expedition." So I sat down, and he entered his dwelling, or said: his lodging. I asked permission to see him, and he permitted me. I entered and greeted him, and he said: "Was there anything between you and Tamim?" I said: "Yes, and we had the upper hand over them. I passed by an old woman of Banu Tamim who was stranded, and she asked me to carry her to you, and here she is at the door." He permitted her, and she entered. I said: "O Messenger of God, if you see fit to make a barrier between us and Tamim, then make it al-Dahna'." The old woman grew angry and rose quickly and said: "O Messenger of God, then where will your distressed one (*mudtarr*) go?" He said: I said: "My example is that of what the first one said: 'A goat that carried its own death.' I carried this one without realizing she was an adversary to me. I seek refuge in God and His Messenger from being like the envoy of 'Ad." He said: "Go on, and what was the envoy of 'Ad?"—and he knew the story better than him, but he wanted him to recount it. I said: "'Ad suffered drought, so they sent an envoy named Qayl. He passed by Mu'awiyah ibn Bakr and stayed with him for a month, being given wine to drink while two slave-girls called 'al-Jaradatan' sang to him. When the month passed, he went out to the mountains of Mahrah and said: 'O God, You know that I have not come to a sick person to treat him, nor to a captive to ransom him. O God, give 'Ad to drink as You used to give them.' Then dark clouds passed by him, and he was called from among them: 'Choose.' He pointed to a black cloud among them, and he was called from it: 'Take it as ashes, scattering, leaving none of 'Ad alive.'" He said: "It was not reported to me that any wind was sent upon them except as much as flows through this ring of mine, until they perished." Abu Wa'il said: "And he spoke the truth." And when they sent an envoy among them, the man and the woman would say: "Do not be like the envoy of 'Ad."

Al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it, as has passed in surah al-A'raf.[[Al-Musnad (3/482); see the takhrij of the rest of this hadith under verse 73 of surah al-A'raf.]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us; Ibn Wahb informed us; 'Amr informed us, that Abu al-Nadr narrated to him, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from 'A'ishah[[In T: "'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her."]], that she said: "I never saw the Messenger of God (ﷺ) laughing so fully that I could see his uvula; he only smiled." She said: "And when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) saw a cloud or wind, it was recognized in his face." She said: "O Messenger of God, people rejoice when they see a cloud, hoping it will bring rain, but I see you, when you see it, recognize aversion in your face?" He said: "O 'A'ishah, what assures me that there is not in it a punishment? A people were punished by wind, and a people saw the punishment and said: 'This is a cloud bringing us rain.'" Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it from the narration of Ibn Wahb.[[Al-Musnad (6/66); Sahih al-Bukhari (4828, 4829); Sahih Muslim (899).]]

Another route: Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh, from his father, from 'A'ishah, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) whenever he saw a rising cloud on one of the horizons of the sky, would leave his work, even if he was in prayer, then say: "O God, I seek refuge in You from the evil that is in it."[[In M: "min su' 'aqibatihi" (from the evil of its consequence).]] If God removed it, he praised God, and if it rained he said: "O God, let it be a beneficial rain."[[Al-Musnad (6/190).]]

Another route: Muslim said in his Sahih: Abu al-Tahir narrated to us; Ibn Wahb informed us; I heard Ibn Jurayj narrating from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from 'A'ishah, who said: "When the wind blew strongly, the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) would say: 'O God, I ask You for its good, and the good of what is in it, and the good of what it was sent with, and I seek refuge in You from its evil, and the evil of what is in it, and the evil of what it was sent with.'" She said: "And when the sky became overcast, his colour changed, and he would go out and come in, and advance and withdraw. When it rained, he was relieved, and 'A'ishah recognized that, so she asked him, and he said: 'Perhaps, O 'A'ishah, it is as the people of 'Ad said: ﴿When they saw it as a cloud coming toward their valleys, they said: This is a cloud bringing us rain﴾."[[Sahih Muslim (899).]]

We have mentioned the story of the destruction of 'Ad in the two surahs al-A'raf and Hud, which is sufficient so that it need not be repeated here, and to God belongs praise and favour.

Al-Tabarani said: 'Abdan ibn Ahmad narrated to us; Isma'il ibn Zakariyya al-Kufi narrated to us; Abu Malik narrated to us, from Muslim al-Mula'i, from Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr,[[In T: "And al-Tabarani narrated with his chain."]] from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Only the size of a ring's opening of wind was released upon 'Ad. Then it was sent upon them, carrying them [from] the desert to the settled lands. When the people of the settled lands saw it, they said: 'This is a cloud bringing us rain, approaching our valleys.' The people of the desert were in it, so the people of the desert were thrown upon the people of the settled lands until they perished. He said: It rose over its keepers until it came out through the cracks of the doors."[[In T: "houses."]][[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/42). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/113): "In it is Muslim al-Mula'i, who is weak."]]

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 46, verses 26–28:

He, exalted is He, says: We had established the earlier nations on earth in respect of wealth and children, and We gave them of it what We have not given you, nor anything close to it. ﴿And We made for them hearing and sight and hearts, but their hearing and their sight and their hearts availed them nothing at all, since they used to deny the signs of Allah, and there encompassed them that which they used to mock.﴾ That is: the punishment and retribution that they used to deny and consider unlikely to occur encompassed them. In other words: beware, O you who are addressed, lest you become like them, and there befall you the like of the punishment that befell them in this world and the Hereafter.

* *

His saying: ﴿And We had destroyed the towns around you﴾ means the people of Makkah. Allah destroyed the nations that denied the messengers from around them, such as 'Ad, who were in al-Ahqaf in Hadramawt near Yemen, and Thamud, whose dwellings lay between them and al-Sham. Likewise Saba', who were the people of Yemen, and Madyan, which lay on their route and path to Gaza. Likewise the Dead Sea of the people of Lut, which they also passed by.

* *

His saying: ﴿And We varied the signs﴾ means: We made them clear and explained them, ﴿so that they might return.﴾ ﴿Why then did those whom they had taken as gods besides Allah, as a means of nearness, not help them?⁠﴾ That is: why did they not help them when they were in need of them? ﴿Rather, they vanished from them⁠﴾ means: rather, they were gone from them at the time they most needed them. ﴿That was their falsehood⁠﴾ means: their lie, ﴿and what they used to fabricate⁠﴾ means: and their fabrication in taking them as gods. They were indeed ruined and lost in their worship of them and their reliance upon them.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 46, verses 29–32 (part 1 of 5):

Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, 'Amr narrated to us: I heard Ikrimah, from al-Zubayr, regarding ﴿And when We turned towards you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an﴾ [al-Ahqaf 46:29]. He said: "At Nakhla, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was praying the late night prayer (al-'Isha' al-Akhirah), ﴿they were nearly crowding upon him﴾ [al-Jinn 72:19]." Sufyan said: "al-Libad means some of them upon others, like the layers of a felt (al-libad) upon one another." [[al-Musnad (1/167).]]

Ahmad alone narrated this. It will come from the narration of Ibn Jarir, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that they were seven men from the jinn of Nasibin.

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Affan narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us (ḥ). The renowned hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said in his book Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (Proofs of Prophethood): Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abdan informed us, Ahmad ibn 'Ubayd al-Saffar informed us, Isma'il al-Qadi narrated to us, Musaddad informed us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not recite to the jinn, nor did he see them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out with a group of his companions intending the market of 'Ukaz. The devils had been prevented from receiving news of the heavens, and shooting stars were sent against them. The devils returned to their people and said: "What is wrong with you?" They said: "We have been prevented from receiving news of the heavens, and shooting stars have been sent against us." They said: "Nothing has come between you and the news of the heavens except something that has happened. So strike the eastern and western parts of the earth and see what this is that has come between you and the news of the heavens." So they set out, striking the eastern and western parts of the earth, seeking what this was that had come between them and the news of the heavens. That company who had headed towards Tihama turned back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who was at Nakhla, intending the market of 'Ukaz, and he was leading his companions in the dawn prayer. When they heard the Qur'an, they listened to it and said: "This, by Allah, is what has come between you and the news of the heavens." Then, when they returned to their people, they said: "O our people, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, guiding to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord." And Allah revealed to His Prophet [[In T, M, A: "His Prophet ﷺ."]]: ﴿Say: It has been revealed to me that a company of the jinn listened﴾ [al-Jinn 72:1]. What was revealed to him was only the statement of the jinn. [[al-Musnad (1/252), and Dala'il al-Nubuwwah lil-Bayhaqi (2/225).]]

It was narrated by al-Bukhari from Musaddad in similar wording, and Muslim narrated it from Shaybān ibn Farrukh, from Abu 'Awanah, with the same. al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in their books of tafsir also narrated it from the hadith of Abu 'Awanah. [[Sahih al-Bukhari (no. 773), Sahih Muslim (no. 449), Sunan al-Tirmidhi (no. 3323), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (no. 1164).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The jinn used to listen to the revelation, and they would hear a word and add ten words to it. What they heard was true, but what they added was false. Before that, the stars were not thrown at them. But when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent, whenever one of them came to his seat he would be struck by a flame that would burn whatever it hit." They complained of this to Iblis, who said: "This is only due to a matter that has occurred." So he dispatched his troops, and behold, the Prophet ﷺ was praying between the two mountains of Nakhla. They came to him and informed him, and he said: "This is the event that has occurred on the earth."

al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in the books of tafsir of their Sunan narrated it from the hadith of Isra'il with this chain. al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih." [[Sahih al-Bukhari (no. 773), Sahih Muslim (no. 449), Sunan al-Tirmidhi (no. 3323), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (no. 1164).]]

Similarly, Ayyub narrated it from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas. Likewise, al-'Awfi narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas also, with the same full context. Similarly, al-Hasan al-Basri said that he (peace be upon him) did not perceive their matter until Allah revealed to him their news.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned, from Yazid ibn Ruman, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, the story of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ going out to al-Ta'if, his calling them to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and their refusal of him. He related the story in full and cited that beautiful supplication: "O Allah, to You I complain of the weakness of my strength and the scarcity of my resources," until its end. He said: When he turned away from them, he spent the night at Nakhla, and he recited Qur'an that night, and the jinn of the people of Nasibin listened to him. [[See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah li-Ibn Hisham (1/419).]]

This is authentic, but his statement, "The jinn's listening was that night," is open to question, because the jinn's listening was at the beginning of the revelation, as indicated by the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas mentioned above. His (peace be upon him) going out to al-Ta'if was after the death of his uncle, and that was a year or two before the Hijrah, as Ibn Ishaq and others established. [And Allah knows best.] [[Addition from T.]]

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Zirr [[In T: "Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah also narrated with his chain."]], from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "They descended upon the Prophet ﷺ while he was reciting the Qur'an in the valley of Nakhla. When they heard it, they said: 'Be silent.' He said: 'Quiet.' They were nine, one of them being Zawba'ah." So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And when We turned towards you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an. When they attended it, they said, "Be silent." When it was concluded, they went back to their people as warners﴾ up to: ﴿in clear error﴾ [al-Ahqaf 46:29–31 (part)]. [[al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/456) through the route of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, and said: "Its chain is sahih, but they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed.]]

This, together with the first narration from Ibn 'Abbas, implies that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not perceive their presence on this occasion, and they only listened to his recitation, then returned to their people. After that, they came to him in groups, one people after another, and company after company, as the reports and narrations will be given in their place, which we will mention here, if Allah wills, and in Him is trust.

As for what al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated from Abu Qudamah 'Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id al-Sarkhasi, from Abu Usamah Hammad ibn Usamah, from Mis'ar ibn Kidam, from Ma'n ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: "I heard my father say: I asked Masruq: 'Who informed the Prophet ﷺ on the night they listened to the Qur'an?' He said: 'Your father (meaning Ibn Mas'ud) told me that a tree informed him about them.'" [[Sahih al-Bukhari (no. 3859), Sahih Muslim (no. 450).]] This may be the first occasion, and it would be an affirmation that takes precedence over Ibn 'Abbas's negation. It may also be one of the later occasions, and Allah knows best. It is also possible that it was the first occasion but he did not perceive them while they were listening, until the tree informed him of them, meaning it informed him of their listening, and Allah knows best.

al-Hafiz al-Bayhaqi said: What Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, related is only about the first time the jinn heard the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and learned his condition. At that time he had not recited to them nor seen them. Then after that, a summoner of the jinn came to him, and he recited the Qur'an to them and called them to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as narrated by 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him. [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah lil-Bayhaqi (2/227).]]

Mention of the narration from him regarding that:
