While I was sleeping near their idols, a man came with a calf and slaughtered it, and a shouter shouted at him, a shout I had never heard louder than it, saying: "O Jalih, a successful affair, a man eloquent says: 'There is no god but Allah.'" The people leapt up, and I said: "I will not leave until I know what lies behind this." Then he called again: "O Jalih, a successful affair, a man eloquent says: 'There is no god but Allah.'" So I got up, and not long after it was said: "This is a Prophet."'"

This is the wording of al-Bukhari. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3866).]] Al-Bayhaqi related it from the hadith of Ibn Wahb, with similar wording, then said: "The apparent meaning of this report suggests that 'Umar himself heard the shouter crying out from the calf that was slaughtered, and likewise it is explicit in a weak report from 'Umar concerning his Islam, but all the other reports indicate that this soothsayer is the one who related that from his seeing and hearing, and Allah knows best." [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (2/245).]]

What al-Bayhaqi said is the most plausible. This man is Sawad ibn Qarib, and I have mentioned this in detail in the biography of 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, so whoever wants it should take it from there, and to Allah belongs all praise [and grace]. [[Addition from A.]]

Al-Bayhaqi said: "The hadith of Sawad ibn Qarib, and it may be that this is the soothsayer whose name was not mentioned in the authentic hadith."

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Habib al-Mufassir informed us, from the original of his hearing; Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Saffar al-Asbahani informed us, by reading to him: Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Musa al-Hammar al-Kufi narrated to us in Kufa; Ziyad ibn Yazid ibn Badawayh Abu Bakr al-Qasri narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Nawwas al-Kufi narrated to us; Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from T.]] who said: "While 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was delivering a sermon to the people from the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: 'O people, is Sawad ibn Qarib among you?' No one answered him that year. When the following year came, he said: 'O people, is Sawad ibn Qarib among you?' I said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, who is Sawad ibn Qarib?' 'Umar said to him: 'Sawad ibn Qarib's beginning of Islam was something amazing.' While we were in that state, Sawad ibn Qarib appeared, and 'Umar said to him: 'O Sawad, tell us about the beginning of your Islam, how was it?' Sawad said: 'I was staying in India, and I had a jinn companion. One night while I was sleeping, he came to me in that dream and said: "Arise, understand and reflect, if you are able to reflect, a messenger has been sent from Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib." Then he began to recite:

'I am amazed at the jinn and their vile ones, and their binding of camels with their saddle-cloths,
they fly towards Makkah seeking guidance; the believers among the jinn are not like their wicked ones.
So rise up towards the elite of Hashim, and wipe your eyes towards its head.'

He said: Then he woke me and frightened me, and said: 'O Sawad ibn Qarib, Allah has sent a Prophet, so rise towards him and you will be guided and rightly guided.' When it was the second night, he came to me, woke me, then began to recite similarly:

'I am amazed at the jinn and their pursuit, and their binding of camels with their saddles,
they fly towards Makkah seeking guidance; their leader is not like their tail.
So rise up towards the elite of Hashim, and wipe your eyes towards its fang.'

When it was the third night, he came to me, woke me, then said:

'I am amazed at the jinn and their knowledge of them, and their binding of camels with their pack-saddles,
they fly towards Makkah seeking guidance; those of evil are not like their righteous.
So rise up towards the elite of Hashim; the believers among the jinn are not like their disbelievers.'"

He said: When I heard it repeated night after night, the love of Islam entered my heart, by the will of Allah, from the matter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: I set off to my saddlebag, fastened it onto my riding camel, and had not yet untied one knot or tied another when I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He was in Al-Madinah, meaning Makkah, and the people around him were crowded like the mane of a horse. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw me, he said: "Welcome, O Sawad ibn Qarib. We already know what brought you." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have composed a poem, so let me recite it to you." Sawad said: I said:

*A visitor came to me after the first part of the night and sleep, and what I have experienced of him has never been a lie.*

*Three nights, his words each night: "A messenger has come to you from Luayy ibn Ghalib."*

*So I hitched up my izar above my shin and I was carried by a strong, swift she-camel among the open plains.*

*I bear witness that Allah, there is nothing besides Him, and that you are trusted over every unseen matter.*

*And that you are the nearest of the messengers in intercession to Allah, O son of the most noble and the purest.*

*So command us with what has come to you, O best of messengers, even if what came is grey-haired in its locks.*

*And be my intercessor on a day when no one has intercession except you, one who is sufficient in place of Sawad ibn Qarib.*

He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed until his molar teeth showed, and he said to me: "You have succeeded, O Sawad." Then Umar said to him: "Does your visitor still come to you now?" He said: "Since I recited the Qur'an, he has not come to me, and the Book of Allah is a better replacement for the jinn." (Dala'il al-nubuwwah by al-Bayhaqi, 1/248.)

Then al-Bayhaqi narrated it through two other chains. Among what indicates their delegation to him (peace be upon him) after he migrated to Al-Madinah is the report narrated by the hafiz (memorizer of hadith) Abu Nu'aym in his book Dala'il al-nubuwwah, saying:

Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Abdah al-Misisi narrated to us: Abu Tawbah al-Rabi' ibn Nafi' narrated to us: Mu'awiyah ibn Sallam narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, that he heard Abu Sallam say: "Someone who was told by Amr ibn Ghaylan al-Thaqafi narrated to me, saying: I came to Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and said to him: 'I have been told that you were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the delegation of the jinn.' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Tell me how the matter was.' He said: 'The People of the Suffah each took a man to feed him, and I was left, and none of them took me. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by me and said: "Who is this?" I said: "I am Ibn Mas'ud." He said: "Did no one take you to feed you?" I said: "No." He said: "Come along, perhaps I will find something for you." So we went until he came to the room of Umm Salamah, and he left me and entered among his family. Then a young servant girl came out and said: "O Ibn Mas'ud, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has not found supper for you, so return to your resting place." So I returned to the mosque, gathered the pebbles of the mosque, used them as a pillow, and wrapped myself in my garment. I had not waited long when the girl came and said: "Answer the call of the Messenger of Allah." So I followed her, hoping for supper, until when I reached my place, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out with a palm-frond stalk in his hand, placed it against my chest and said: "Will you go with me wherever I go?" I said: "As Allah wills." He repeated it to me three times, and each time I said: "As Allah wills." So he set off and I set off with him until we came to the Baqi' al-Gharqad. He drew a line with his staff and said: "Sit within it, and do not leave until I come to you." Then he walked on while I watched him between the palm trees, until, when he was out of my sight, a black dust cloud rose. I became frightened and said: "I will go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for I think Hawazin have plotted against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to kill him, so I will run to the houses and seek help from the people." But I remembered that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had instructed me not to leave the place where I was. Then I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) striking them with his staff and saying: "Sit down!" So they sat down until the column of dawn was almost splitting, then they rose and left. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to me and said: "Did you sleep after me?" I said: "No. By Allah, I was terrified with the first fright, to the point that I thought of going to the houses to seek help from the people, until I heard you striking them with your staff. I had thought it was Hawazin who had plotted against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to kill him." He said: "Had you left this circle, I would not have been secure for you from some of them snatching you. Did you see anything of them?" I said: "I saw black men with white garments tucked up." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Those were the delegation of the jinn of Nasibin. They came to me and asked me for provisions and goods, so I provided them with every bone that is bare, or dung, or droppings." I said: "And what good does that do them?" He said: "They never find a bone without finding on it the meat that was on it on the day it was eaten, and no dung without finding in it the grain that was in it the day it was eaten. So let none of you purify himself with a bone or droppings."' (I have not found this in the printed Dala'il al-nubuwwah of Abu Nu'aym.)"

This is a very strange chain, but it contains an unnamed man who is not identified [and Allah knows best]. Abu Nu'aym also narrated, from the hadith of Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid: Numayr ibn Zayd al-Qanbar narrated to me: my father narrated to us: Qahafah ibn Rabi'ah narrated to us: al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led us in the dawn prayer in the mosque of Al-Madinah, and when he finished he said: "Which of you will follow me to the delegation of the jinn tonight?" The people remained silent three times. Then he passed by me, took my hand, and I began walking with him until all the mountains of Al-Madinah were hidden from us, and we reached an open land. Suddenly there were tall men like spears, their garments tucked up between their legs. When I saw them, a violent trembling overtook me. Then he mentioned something similar to the earlier hadith of Ibn Mas'ud. (I have not found this in the printed Dala'il al-nubuwwah of Abu Nu'aym.) This is a strange hadith, and Allah knows best.

Among what relates to the delegation of the jinn is what Abu Nu'aym, the hafiz, narrated: Abu Muhammad ibn Hayyan narrated to us: Abu al-Tayyib Ahmad ibn Rawh narrated to us: Ya'qub al-Dawraqi narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Bukayr al-Tamimi narrated to us: Husayn ibn Umar (in one manuscript, "Umayr") narrated to us, and Ubayd al-Muktib informed me, from Ibrahim, who said: A group of the companions of Abdullah (in one manuscript, "Ubaydullah") set out wishing to perform Hajj. When they were on part of the road, they came upon a snake crawling across the road, white, from which the scent of musk was exhaling. I said to my companions: "Go on, for I will not leave until I see what becomes of this snake." He said: It did not remain long before it died. So I went to a white cloth, wrapped it in it, moved it off the road, and buried it. Then I caught up with my companions at the evening meal. He said: By Allah, we were sitting when four women came from the direction of the west. One of them said: "Which of you buried Amr?" We said: "Who is Amr?" She said: "Which of you buried the snake?" I said: "I did." She said: "By Allah, you buried a man who fasted often and prayed at night often, who commanded what Allah had revealed, and he believed in your Prophet and heard his description from the sky four hundred years before he was sent." The man said: We praised Allah, then completed our Hajj. Then I passed by Umar ibn al-Khattab in Al-Madinah and informed him of the matter of the snake. He said: "You have spoken truly. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'He believed in me four hundred years before I was sent.'" (Dala'il al-nubuwwah of Abu Nu'aym, p. 306.)

This is a very strange hadith, and Allah knows best.

Abu Nu'aym said: al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from al-Sha'bi, from a man of Thaqif, something similar. Abdullah ibn Ahmad and al-Zahrani narrated from Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal, the one who descended and buried that snake among the Companions, and that they said: "Indeed, he is the last of the nine who died among those who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) listening to the Qur'an." (I have not found this in the printed Dala'il al-nubuwwah of Abu Nu'aym.)

Abu Nu'aym also narrated, from the hadith of al-Layth ibn Sa'd, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Salamah al-Majishun, from his paternal uncle, from Mu'adh ibn Ubaydullah (in other manuscripts, "Abdullah") ibn Ma'mar, who said: I was sitting with Uthman ibn Affan when a man came and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, I was in a desert wasteland," and he mentioned that he saw two serpents (in other manuscripts, "two whirlwinds") fighting until one of them killed the other. He said: I went to the battlefield and found many dead snakes, and from some of them came the scent of musk. I began smelling them one by one until I found that scent from a thin, yellow snake. I wrapped it in my turban and buried it. As I was walking, a caller called to me (in one manuscript, "this is a jinn"): "O Abdullah, you have been guided! These are two groups of the jinn, the sons of Ash'iban and the sons of Uqaysh, who met, and what you saw of the dead occurred. The one you buried was martyred, and he was among those who heard the revelation from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He said: Uthman said to that man: "If you are truthful, then you have seen a wonder, and if you are lying, then your lie is upon you." (Dala'il al-nubuwwah of Abu Nu'aym, p. 305.)

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And [mention] when We turned toward you a group of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an﴾, that is, a company of the jinn. ﴿When they attended it, they said, "Be silent."﴾

That is: listen. And this was courtesy from them.

Al-Hafiz al-Bayhaqi said: Al-Imam Abu al-Tayyib Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman informed us: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Daqqaq informed us: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Bushanji narrated to us: Hisham ibn Ammar al-Dimashqi narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited Surah "al-Rahman" until he finished it, then said: "What is wrong with me that I see you silent? The jinn were better in response than you. Every time I recited to them this verse: ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ they said: 'Nor of any of Your blessings, our Lord, do we deny. So to You is the praise.'"

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Tafsir, from Abu Muslim Abd al-Rahman ibn Waqid, from al-Walid ibn Muslim with the same chain. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to his companions, recited to them Surah al-Rahman, and mentioned it. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib (strange); we do not know it except from the hadith of al-Walid, from Zuhayr," so he said. Al-Bayhaqi also narrated it from the hadith of Marwan ibn Muhammad al-Tatari, from Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, with a similar wording. (Dala'il al-nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi, 1/232, and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3291.)

* *

And His saying: ﴿When it was completed﴾, that is, finished, like His saying: ﴿And when the prayer is concluded﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 10], ﴿So He completed them as seven heavens in two days﴾ [Fussilat: 12], and ﴿And when you have completed your rites﴾ [al-Baqarah: 200]. ﴿They returned to their people as warners﴾, that is, they went back to their people and warned them of what they had heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, like His saying: ﴿So that they may gain understanding of the religion and warn their people when they return to them, that they may beware﴾ [al-Tawbah: 122].

This verse has been used as evidence that there were warners among the jinn, but that there were no messengers among them. There is no doubt that Allah did not send a messenger from among the jinn, as He says: ﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns﴾ [Yusuf: 109], and He says: ﴿And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets﴾ [al-Furqan: 20]. And He said about Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil): ﴿And We placed in his descendants prophethood and the Book﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 27].

So every prophet Allah sent after Abraham was from his descendants and progeny. As for His saying in [Surah] [[Addition from manuscript T.]] al-An'am: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ [al-An'am: 130], the meaning is the two kinds collectively, so it applies to one of them, which is mankind, like His saying: ﴿From both of them emerge the pearl and the coral﴾ [al-Rahman: 22], meaning from one of them.

Then He explained the warning of the jinn to their people, saying as He reports about them: ﴿They said, "O our people, indeed we have heard a Book revealed after Moses [confirming what came before it, guiding to the truth]"﴾ [[Addition from manuscript A.]], and they did not mention Jesus, because the Gospel was revealed to Jesus, peace be upon him, and it contains admonitions, softening of hearts, and a little of what is lawful and unlawful. It is in reality a complement to the law of the Torah, and the foundation is the Torah. For this reason they said: "revealed after Moses." Waraqah ibn Nawfal said the same when the Prophet ﷺ told him the story of Gabriel [peace be upon him] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] coming to him for the first time. He said: "Bakh bakh! This is the namus (the angel of revelation) that used to come to Moses. Would that I were young in it!"

﴿Confirming what came before it﴾, that is, of the Books sent down before it to the prophets. Their saying ﴿guiding to the truth﴾ means in belief and in reports, and ﴿to a straight path﴾ means in deeds. The Qur'an contains two kinds: information and command. Its information is true and its commands are just, as He said: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice﴾ [al-An'am: 115], and He said: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth﴾ [al-Tawbah: 33]. Guidance is beneficial knowledge, and the religion of truth is righteous action. Likewise the jinn said: ﴿guiding to the truth﴾ in matters of belief, and ﴿to a straight path﴾, that is, in practical matters.

﴿O our people, respond to the caller of Allah﴾. In this is an indication that Allah sent Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, to both the two weighty creations (al-thaqalayn), mankind and the jinn, when he called them to Allah, and he recited to them the surah which contains the address to both groups, their obligations, their promise and their warning, and that is Surah al-Rahman. For this reason they said: ﴿Respond to the caller of Allah and believe in him﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿He will forgive you of your sins﴾. It has been said that "min" here is extra (zā'idah), but this is questionable, since its addition in affirmative statements is rare. It has also been said that it retains its original function, of partitioning (lil-tab'id). ﴿And will protect you from a painful punishment﴾, that is, He will shield you from His painful punishment.

Scholars who held that believing jinn do not enter Paradise have used this verse as evidence, saying that the reward of their righteous ones is only to be spared the punishment of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. For this reason they said this in this context, which is a context of boasting and emphasis. If they had a reward for faith greater than this, they would surely have mentioned it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, saying: I was told on the authority of Jarir, from Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The believing jinn will not enter Paradise, because they are from the offspring of Iblis, and the offspring of Iblis will not enter Paradise."

The truth is that their believers, like the believers among mankind, will enter Paradise, as is the view of a group of the early generations (al-salaf). Some of them have used as evidence His saying: ﴿Neither man nor jinn has touched them before them﴾ [al-Rahman: 74], but this argument is questionable. Better than it is His saying: ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens. So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [al-Rahman: 46–47]. Allah has bestowed favor upon both the two weighty creations by making the reward of their righteous ones Paradise. The jinn responded to this verse with a verbal expression of gratitude more eloquent than mankind's, saying: "Nor of Your blessings, our Lord, do we deny anything. To You be praise." Allah would not bestow favor upon them with a reward that they would not receive. Also, if He repays their disbelievers with the Fire, which is a station of justice, then repaying their believers with Paradise, which is a station of grace, is all the more fitting and proper. Another proof of this is the generality of His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have the Gardens of Paradise as lodging﴾ [al-Kahf: 107], and similar verses. I have written a separate treatise on this question, and all praise and grace belong to Allah.

This Paradise continues to have room until Allah creates a new creation for it. Should He not then house in it whoever believed in Him and did righteous deeds? What they mentioned here as the reward for faith, namely the expiation of sins and protection from the painful punishment, necessarily implies entry into Paradise, because in the Hereafter there is only Paradise or the Fire. Whoever is spared the Fire enters Paradise without doubt. We have no explicit or apparent text from the Lawgiver stating that believing jinn will not enter Paradise even if they are spared the Fire. If such a text were authentic, we would adopt it, and Allah knows best.

And this is Noah, peace be upon him, saying to his people: ﴿He will forgive you of your sins and delay you until a specified term﴾ [Nuh: 4]. [[Variant from manuscripts T and A: "wa-yujirakum", which is an error.]] There is no disagreement that the believers among his people are in Paradise, and so are these.

Strange views have been reported about them. From 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz: they will not enter the central part of Paradise (bukhbuhat al-jannah), but will be in its outskirts (rabad), around it and in its edges. Some people claimed that in Paradise they will see the children of Adam while the children of Adam will not see them, the reverse of their situation in this worldly abode. Some people said: they do not eat or drink in Paradise, but are inspired with glorifying, praising and sanctifying God instead of food and drink, like the angels, because they are of the same kind as them. All these views are questionable, and there is no proof for them.

Then He said, reporting about them: ﴿And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah will not escape [Him] on earth﴾, that is, rather, the power of Allah encompasses him and surrounds him. ﴿And he will have no protectors other than Him﴾, that is, no one will shield them from Him. ﴿Those are in manifest error﴾. This is a station of threat and warning. They called their people both with encouragement and with warning, and for this reason many of them responded, and they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in delegations (wufud), delegation after delegation, as has been explained earlier.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 46, verses 29–32 (part 1 of 5):

Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, 'Amr narrated to us: I heard Ikrimah, from al-Zubayr, regarding ﴿And when We turned towards you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an﴾ [al-Ahqaf 46:29]. He said: "At Nakhla, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was praying the late night prayer (al-'Isha' al-Akhirah), ﴿they were nearly crowding upon him﴾ [al-Jinn 72:19]." Sufyan said: "al-Libad means some of them upon others, like the layers of a felt (al-libad) upon one another." [[al-Musnad (1/167).]]

Ahmad alone narrated this. It will come from the narration of Ibn Jarir, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that they were seven men from the jinn of Nasibin.

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Affan narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us (ḥ). The renowned hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said in his book Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (Proofs of Prophethood): Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abdan informed us, Ahmad ibn 'Ubayd al-Saffar informed us, Isma'il al-Qadi narrated to us, Musaddad informed us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not recite to the jinn, nor did he see them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out with a group of his companions intending the market of 'Ukaz. The devils had been prevented from receiving news of the heavens, and shooting stars were sent against them. The devils returned to their people and said: "What is wrong with you?" They said: "We have been prevented from receiving news of the heavens, and shooting stars have been sent against us." They said: "Nothing has come between you and the news of the heavens except something that has happened. So strike the eastern and western parts of the earth and see what this is that has come between you and the news of the heavens." So they set out, striking the eastern and western parts of the earth, seeking what this was that had come between them and the news of the heavens. That company who had headed towards Tihama turned back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who was at Nakhla, intending the market of 'Ukaz, and he was leading his companions in the dawn prayer. When they heard the Qur'an, they listened to it and said: "This, by Allah, is what has come between you and the news of the heavens." Then, when they returned to their people, they said: "O our people, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, guiding to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord." And Allah revealed to His Prophet [[In T, M, A: "His Prophet ﷺ."]]: ﴿Say: It has been revealed to me that a company of the jinn listened﴾ [al-Jinn 72:1]. What was revealed to him was only the statement of the jinn. [[al-Musnad (1/252), and Dala'il al-Nubuwwah lil-Bayhaqi (2/225).]]

It was narrated by al-Bukhari from Musaddad in similar wording, and Muslim narrated it from Shaybān ibn Farrukh, from Abu 'Awanah, with the same. al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in their books of tafsir also narrated it from the hadith of Abu 'Awanah. [[Sahih al-Bukhari (no. 773), Sahih Muslim (no. 449), Sunan al-Tirmidhi (no. 3323), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (no. 1164).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The jinn used to listen to the revelation, and they would hear a word and add ten words to it. What they heard was true, but what they added was false. Before that, the stars were not thrown at them. But when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent, whenever one of them came to his seat he would be struck by a flame that would burn whatever it hit." They complained of this to Iblis, who said: "This is only due to a matter that has occurred." So he dispatched his troops, and behold, the Prophet ﷺ was praying between the two mountains of Nakhla. They came to him and informed him, and he said: "This is the event that has occurred on the earth."

al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in the books of tafsir of their Sunan narrated it from the hadith of Isra'il with this chain. al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih." [[Sahih al-Bukhari (no. 773), Sahih Muslim (no. 449), Sunan al-Tirmidhi (no. 3323), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (no. 1164).]]

Similarly, Ayyub narrated it from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas. Likewise, al-'Awfi narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas also, with the same full context. Similarly, al-Hasan al-Basri said that he (peace be upon him) did not perceive their matter until Allah revealed to him their news.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned, from Yazid ibn Ruman, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, the story of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ going out to al-Ta'if, his calling them to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and their refusal of him. He related the story in full and cited that beautiful supplication: "O Allah, to You I complain of the weakness of my strength and the scarcity of my resources," until its end. He said: When he turned away from them, he spent the night at Nakhla, and he recited Qur'an that night, and the jinn of the people of Nasibin listened to him. [[See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah li-Ibn Hisham (1/419).]]

This is authentic, but his statement, "The jinn's listening was that night," is open to question, because the jinn's listening was at the beginning of the revelation, as indicated by the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas mentioned above. His (peace be upon him) going out to al-Ta'if was after the death of his uncle, and that was a year or two before the Hijrah, as Ibn Ishaq and others established. [And Allah knows best.] [[Addition from T.]]

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Zirr [[In T: "Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah also narrated with his chain."]], from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "They descended upon the Prophet ﷺ while he was reciting the Qur'an in the valley of Nakhla. When they heard it, they said: 'Be silent.' He said: 'Quiet.' They were nine, one of them being Zawba'ah." So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And when We turned towards you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an. When they attended it, they said, "Be silent." When it was concluded, they went back to their people as warners﴾ up to: ﴿in clear error﴾ [al-Ahqaf 46:29–31 (part)]. [[al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/456) through the route of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, and said: "Its chain is sahih, but they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed.]]

This, together with the first narration from Ibn 'Abbas, implies that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not perceive their presence on this occasion, and they only listened to his recitation, then returned to their people. After that, they came to him in groups, one people after another, and company after company, as the reports and narrations will be given in their place, which we will mention here, if Allah wills, and in Him is trust.

As for what al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated from Abu Qudamah 'Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id al-Sarkhasi, from Abu Usamah Hammad ibn Usamah, from Mis'ar ibn Kidam, from Ma'n ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: "I heard my father say: I asked Masruq: 'Who informed the Prophet ﷺ on the night they listened to the Qur'an?' He said: 'Your father (meaning Ibn Mas'ud) told me that a tree informed him about them.'" [[Sahih al-Bukhari (no. 3859), Sahih Muslim (no. 450).]] This may be the first occasion, and it would be an affirmation that takes precedence over Ibn 'Abbas's negation. It may also be one of the later occasions, and Allah knows best. It is also possible that it was the first occasion but he did not perceive them while they were listening, until the tree informed him of them, meaning it informed him of their listening, and Allah knows best.

al-Hafiz al-Bayhaqi said: What Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, related is only about the first time the jinn heard the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and learned his condition. At that time he had not recited to them nor seen them. Then after that, a summoner of the jinn came to him, and he recited the Qur'an to them and called them to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as narrated by 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him. [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah lil-Bayhaqi (2/227).]]

Mention of the narration from him regarding that:

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Dawud narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi (and Ibn Abi Za'idah informed us, Dawud informed us, from al-Sha'bi [[In T: "So Imam Ahmad narrated with his chain."]]), from 'Alqamah, who said: "I said to 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: Was there anyone among you who accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the night of the jinn?" He said: "None of us accompanied him, but we lost him one night in Makkah, and we said: 'Has he been assassinated? Has he been carried off?' What has happened to him?" He said: "So we spent the worst night any people ever spent. When it was at the break of dawn, or he said: at the pre-dawn, behold, we saw him coming from the direction of Hira. We said: 'O Messenger of Allah,' and they mentioned to him what they had been in. He said: 'The summoner of the jinn came to me, so I went to them and recited to them.'" He said: "So he set off, and showed us their traces and the traces of their fires." He said: "al-Sha'bi said: They asked him for provisions." 'Amir said: "They asked him in Makkah, and they were from the jinn of the Peninsula." He said: "He said: 'Every bone over which the name of Allah has been mentioned that falls into your hands will be more meaty than it was, and every dung or dropping will be fodder for your animals.' He said: 'So do not clean yourselves with them, for they are the provision of your brothers among the jinn.'" [[al-Musnad (1/436), and Sahih Muslim (no. 450).]]

Thus Muslim narrated it in his Sahih, from 'Ali ibn Hujr, from Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah, with similar wording. [[al-Musnad (1/436), and Sahih Muslim (no. 450).]]

Muslim also said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Dawud, that is Ibn Abi Hind, narrated to us, from 'Amir, who said: "I asked 'Alqamah: Was Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the night of the jinn?" He said: "'Alqamah said: I asked Ibn Mas'ud: 'Did any of you attend with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the night of the jinn?' He said: 'No, but we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one night, and we lost him, so we searched for him in the valleys and ravines. We said: "Has he been carried off? Has he been assassinated?" So we spent the worst night any people ever spent. When we woke in the morning, behold, he came from the direction of Hira.' He said: 'We said: "O Messenger of Allah, we lost you, we searched for you and did not find you, so we spent the worst night any people ever spent."' He said: 'He said: "The summoner of the jinn came to me, so I went with them, and I recited the Qur'an to them."' He said: 'So he took us along and showed us their traces and the traces of their fires, and they asked him for provisions. He said: "Every bone over which the name of Allah has been mentioned that falls into your hands will be more meaty than it was, and every dung or dropping will be fodder for your animals."' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'So do not clean yourselves with them, for they are the food of your brothers.'" [[Sahih Muslim (no. 450).]]

Another route from Ibn Mas'ud: Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, my paternal uncle narrated to me, Yunus narrated to me, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, that Ibn Mas'ud said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'I spent the night reciting to the jinn a quarter (of the Qur'an) at al-Hajun.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (26/21), and Ahmad in al-Musnad (1/416) through the route of Yunus from al-Zuhri, with the same.]]

Another way: in it, he was with him on the night of the Jinn. Ibn Jarir said, may Allah have mercy on him: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to me, from my paternal uncle ʿAbd Allah ibn Wahb, who said: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu ʿUthman ibn Sunnah al-Khuzaʿi, who was from the people of al-Sham [[In T: "Muslim narrated it, and Ibn Jarir narrated it with his chain."]], that ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions while he was in Makkah: "Whoever among you wishes to attend the affair of the Jinn tonight, let him do so." None of them attended except me. He said: So we set off until, when we were at the upper part of Makkah, he drew a line for me with his foot and then ordered me to sit within it. Then he went off until he stood, and he began to recite the Qur'an. Many dark shapes enveloped him and came between me and him, so that I could not hear his voice. Then they began to disperse, departing like pieces of cloud, until only a group of them remained. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished at dawn, then he went off and relieved himself, then came to me and said: "What became of the group?" I said: "They are those, O Messenger of Allah." So he gave them bones and dung as provision. Then he forbade anyone from cleansing themselves with dung or bone.

Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam, from Abu Zurʿah Wahb Allah ibn Rashid, from Yunus ibn Yazid al-Aili, with the same chain [[Tafsir al-Tabari (26/21)]].

Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, through the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, from al-Layth, from Yunus, with the same [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (2/330); al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/503) through ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih, with the same. Al-Dhahabi said: "It is sahih according to a group."]].

Ishaq ibn Rahawayh narrated, from Jarir, from Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan, from his father, from Ibn Masʿud, something similar to what has preceded [[In its chain is Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan, whom Abu Hatim, al-Nasa'i and Ahmad declared weak. Ibn Hibban said: "He reports alone from his father what has no basis, so he sometimes raises the mursal and attributes to himself the mawquf."]].

The Hafiz Abu Nuʿaym narrated it through Musa ibn ʿUbaydah, from Saʿid ibn al-Harith, from Abu al-Muʿalla [[In A: "Ismaʿil."]], from Ibn Masʿud, and he mentioned something similar as well [[Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/80) through Musa ibn ʿUbaydah al-Rabadhi, with the same.]].

Another way: Abu Nuʿaym said: Abu Bakr ibn Malik narrated to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, my father narrated to me, saying: ʿAffan and ʿIkrimah narrated to us, saying: Muʿtamir narrated to us, saying: My father said: Abu Tamimah narrated to me, from ʿAmr — and perhaps he was al-Bikali — whom ʿAmr narrated to him, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked me to follow him, so we set out until we came to such-and-such a place. He drew a line for me and said: "Stay within this line and do not leave it, for if you leave it, you will perish." Then he mentioned the hadith in full, and in it there is great strangeness [[Not found in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah; it is in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad (1/399)]].

Another way: Ibn Jarir said: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir [[In T: "Ibn Jarir narrated it with his chain."]], from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn Ghaylan al-Thaqafi, that he said to Ibn Masʿud: "I have been told that you were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the delegation of the Jinn?" He said: "Yes." He said: "So how was it?" Then he mentioned the whole hadith, and he mentioned that the Prophet (ﷺ) drew a line around him and said: "Do not leave it." Then he mentioned like a black dust-cloud that enveloped the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he was frightened three times. Then, when it was near dawn, the Prophet [[In M: "Messenger of Allah."]] (ﷺ) came to me and said: "Did you sleep?" I said: "No, by Allah, and I have intended several times to call out to the people, until I heard you rebuking them with your staff, saying: 'Sit down!'" He said: "Had you come out, I would not have been safe from some of them snatching you [[In A: "yakhtatifak."]]." Then he said: "Did you see anything?" I said: "Yes, I saw black men with white garments [[In T and A: "mustathfirin."]]." He said: "Those were the Jinn of Nasibin, who asked me for provision — and al-Mata' is provision — so I provided them with every decayed bone, or a dung-pellet or a dropping." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, and what benefit does that bring them?" He said: "They do not find a bone but they find on it its meat on the day it was eaten, and not a dropping but they find in it its grain on the day it was eaten. So let none of you cleanse himself with a bone, a dung-pellet, or a dropping when he comes out of the toilet."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (26/21)]].

Another way: Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami and Abu Nasr ibn Qatadah informed us, both saying: Abu Muhammad Yahya ibn Mansur al-Qadi informed us, Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Bushanji narrated to us, Rawh ibn Salah narrated to us, Musa ibn ʿAli ibn Rabah narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked me to follow him and said: "A party of the Jinn — fifteen, brothers and cousins — come to me tonight, and I recite the Qur'an to them." So I set out with him to the place he intended. He drew a line for me and seated me within it, and said to me: "Do not leave this." So I spent the night within it until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to me at the last part of the night, with a decayed bone in his hand and a black charred dropping. He said to me: "When you go to the toilet, do not cleanse yourself with any of these." He said: When I woke in the morning, I said: "I will certainly find out where the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was," so I went and saw the resting place of sixty camels [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (2/231)]].

Another way: Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Hafiz informed us, Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Asamm informed us, al-ʿAbbas ibn Muhammad al-Duri narrated to us, ʿUthman ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, from al-Mustamirr ibn al-Rayyan, from Abu al-Jawza', from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, who said: I set out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the Jinn, until he reached al-Hajun. He drew a line for me, then he went forward toward them, and they crowded around him. A leader of theirs called Wardan said: "I will remove them from you." But he said: "No one will protect me from Allah [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (2/231)]]."

Another way: Imam Ahmad said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Fazarah al-ʿAbsi, Abu Zayd narrated to us — the client of ʿAmr ibn Huraith — from Ibn Masʿud, who said: When it was the night of the Jinn, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: "Do you have water with you?" I said: "I have no water with me, but I have a water-skin with nabidh in it." The Prophet said: "A good date and pure water," and he performed ablution with it.

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it through the hadith of Abu Zayd, with the same [[Musnad (1/449); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (84); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (88); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (384)]].

Another way: Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn Lahiʿah informed us, from Qays ibn al-Hajjaj, from Hanash al-San'ani, from Ibn ʿAbbas, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, that he was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the Jinn, and the Messenger of Allah said: "O ʿAbd Allah, do you have water with you?" He said: "I have nabidh in a water-skin." He said: "Pour it over me." So he performed ablution, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O ʿAbd Allah, a drink and a purifier [[Musnad (1/398); Ibn Lahiʿah alone narrated it, and he is weak.]]."

Ahmad alone narrated it through this route, and al-Daraqutni narrated it through another route, from Ibn Masʿud [[bihi — addition from M]] [[Sunan al-Daraqutni (1/77) through Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from ʿAmir ibn ʿAlqamah ibn Qays, who said: I said to ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud: "Did any of you witness the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night the caller of the Jinn came to him?" He said: "No." Al-Daraqutni said: "This is the sahih from Ibn Masʿud."]].

Another way: Imam Ahmad said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, my father informed me from Mina', from ʿAbd Allah, who said: I was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the delegation of the Jinn. When he turned away, he sighed, so I said: "What is your condition?" He said: "My soul has been announced to me, O Ibn Masʿud."

Thus I saw it in the Musnad abridged [[Musnad (1/449)]]. The Hafiz Abu Nuʿaym narrated it in his book Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, saying: Sulayman ibn Ahmad ibn Ayyub narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us — and Abu Bakr ibn Malik narrated to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, my father narrated to us, both saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from his father, from Mina', from Ibn Masʿud, who said: I was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the delegation of the Jinn, and he sighed, so I said: "What is wrong with you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "My soul has been announced to me, O Ibn Masʿud." I said: "Appoint a successor." He said: "Who?" I said: "Abu Bakr." He was silent, then he went on for a while and sighed, so I said: "What is your condition, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "My soul has been announced to me, O Ibn Masʿud." I said: "Appoint a successor." He said: "Who?" I said: "ʿUmar [ibn al-Khattab]." He was silent, then he went on for a while, then he sighed, so I said: "What is your condition?" He said: "My soul has been announced to me." I said: "Then appoint a successor." He said (ﷺ): "Who?" I said: "ʿAli ibn Abi Talib." He (ﷺ) said: "As for He in whose hand is my soul, if they obey him, they will enter Paradise all together, one after another [[al-Tabarani, al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/82); in its chain is Maysarah ibn Abi Maysarah, a liar.]]."

This is a very strange hadith, and it is more fitting that it not be preserved. Even if it is sound, the apparent meaning is that this was after their delegation to him in Madinah, as we will mention, for at that time, at the end of the matter, when Makkah was conquered, the people and the Jinn too entered the religion of Allah in multitudes, and the chapter (Surah) [[In T: "Surat al-Nasr."]] was revealed: ﴿When the help of Allah comes and the victory, and you see people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes, then glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance.﴾ It is the surah in which his noble soul was announced to him, as Ibn ʿAbbas stated explicitly, and ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab agreed with him on it. A hadith about this has been transmitted, which we will mention when explaining it, and Allah knows best.

Abu Nuʿaym also narrated it from al-Tabarani, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Hadrami, from ʿAli ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi Burdah, from Yahya ibn Saʿid [[In A: "Yaʿla."]] al-Aslami, from Harb ibn Subayh, from Saʿid ibn Maslamah, from Abu Murrah al-San'ani, from Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Jadali, from Ibn Masʿud, and he mentioned it and mentioned in it the story of the succession [[al-Tabarani, al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/81); in its chain is Yahya al-Aslami, who is weak.]]. This is a strange chain and a wondrous account.

Another way: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Saʿid narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAli ibn Zayd, from Abu Rafiʿ, from Ibn Masʿud, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) [[In M and A: "that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the Jinn."]] drew a line around him, and one of them [[In A: "one of them would come."]] would be like the blackness of bees, and he said to me: "Do not leave your place," and he recited to them the Book of Allah. When he saw the Zutt, he said: "It is as if they were these." And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do you have water with you?" I said: "No." He said: "Do you have nabidh with you?" I said: "Yes." So he performed ablution with it [[Musnad (1/455)]].

Another route, a *mursal* (a report whose chain omits the Companion): Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Zahrani [[In M: "al-Tabarani".]] narrated to us; Hafs ibn 'Umar al-'Adani informed us; al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from Ikrimah, regarding His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And when We turned towards you a company of the jinn﴾. He said: "They were twelve thousand. They came from the island of Mosul. The Prophet ﷺ said to Ibn Mas'ud: 'Wait for me until I come to you,' and he drew a line around him and said: 'Do not leave until I come to you.' When Ibn Mas'ud feared them, he almost went away, but he remembered the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and did not leave. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: 'Had you gone, we would not have met until the Day of Resurrection.'" [[In its chain is al-Hakam ibn Aban, and he is weak.]]

Another route, also *mursal*: Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated from Qatadah, regarding His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And when We turned towards you a company of the jinn﴾: "It was mentioned to us that they were turned towards him from Nineveh, and that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: 'I have been commanded to recite to the jinn, so which of you will follow me?' They lowered their heads. Then he invited them again, and they lowered their heads. Then he invited them a third time, and a man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, that one has a mark (*nudbah*) on him.' So Ibn Mas'ud, the brother of Hudhayl, followed him. He said: The Prophet ﷺ entered a mountain pass called 'Shi'b al-Hajun,' and drew a line around him, and drew a line around Ibn Mas'ud to keep him steady. He said: I began to look, and I saw the likes of vultures moving in their wings, and I heard a loud clamour until I feared for the Prophet of Allah ﷺ. Then he recited the Qur'an. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned, I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what was the clamour I heard?' He said: 'They disputed over a slain man, and judgement was passed between them with truth.'" Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (26/20).]]

All these routes indicate that he ﷺ went to the jinn deliberately, recited the Qur'an to them, called them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and Allah legislated for them through his tongue what they needed at that time. It is possible that the first time they heard him reciting the Qur'an, he did not perceive them, as Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said; then after that they came to him as Ibn Mas'ud related. As for Ibn Mas'ud, he was not with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during his addressing of the jinn and calling them, but was far from him, and no one went out with the Prophet ﷺ except him, and even so he did not witness the addressing. This is the view of al-Bayhaqi.

It is also possible that the first time he went out to them, Ibn Mas'ud was not with him nor anyone else, as is the apparent context of the first report, through the route of Imam Ahmad, which is also in Muslim. Then after that he went out with him another night, and Allah knows best, as Ibn Abi Hatim related in his *Tafsir* on ﴿Say: It has been revealed to me﴾, from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj who said: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Umar said: As for the jinn who met him at Nakhlah, they were the jinn of Nineveh, and as for the jinn who met him in Makkah, they were the jinn of Nusaybin. Al-Bayhaqi interpreted it as meaning: "We spent the worst night that a people ever spent," referring to someone other than Ibn Mas'ud who did not know of the Prophet's ﷺ going out to the jinn. This is possible but far-fetched, and Allah knows best.

The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Abu 'Amr Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Adib informed us; Abu Bakr al-Isma'ili informed us; al-Hasan ibn Sufyan informed us; Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to me; 'Amr ibn Yahya narrated to us, from his grandfather Sa'id ibn 'Amr, who said: [[In A: "'Abd al-Wahhab".]] [[In T: "And al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said with his chain".]] Abu Hurayrah used to follow the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a water vessel for his ablution and his need. One day he caught up with him, and he said: "Who is this?" He said: "I am Abu Hurayrah." He said: "Bring me stones with which to cleanse myself, and do not bring me a bone or dung." So I brought him stones in my garment and placed them beside him. When he finished and stood up, I followed him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the matter with the bone and the dung?" He said: "A delegation of the jinn of Nusaybin came to me and asked me for provision, so I prayed to Allah for them that they should not pass by a bone or dung without finding it as food." [[In T: "al-Rawth".]] [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (2/233).]]

Al-Bukhari narrated it in his *Sahih*, from Musa ibn Isma'il, from 'Amr ibn Yahya, with a chain close to this. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3860).]] This, together with what preceded, indicates that they came to him as a delegation after that. We will mention what indicates that this happened repeatedly.

It has been reported from Ibn 'Abbas other than what was mentioned from him earlier, through a good route. Ibn Jarir said:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us; 'Abd al-Hamid al-Himmani narrated to us; al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: ﴿And when We turned towards you a company of the jinn﴾, to the end of the verse, [he said] [[Addition from A.]]: "They were seven men from the people of Nusaybin, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made them messengers to their people." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (26/22).]]

This indicates that he related both stories.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us; Suwayd ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us; a man whom he named narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And when We turned towards you a company of the jinn﴾, to the end of the verse: "They were seven men: three from the people of Harran and four from the people of Nusaybin. Their names were Hayy, Hasa, Masa, Shasir, Nasir, al-Aradd, Ibyan and al-Ahqam."

Abu Hamzah al-Thumali mentioned that this tribe of the jinn were called the Banu al-Shaysaban; they were the most numerous of the jinn and the noblest in lineage, and they were the main body of Iblis's armies.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from 'Asim, from Dharr, from Ibn Mas'ud: "They were nine, one of them was Zawba'ah. They came to him from the root of Nakhlah."

It was previously reported from him that they were fifteen, and in another narration that they were on sixty mounts. It was previously reported from him that the name of their leader was Wardan. It was said that they were three hundred. And it was previously reported from Ikrimah that they were twelve thousand. Perhaps this difference is evidence that their delegations to him, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, were repeated. Among what indicates this is what al-Bukhari related in his *Sahih*:

Yahya ibn Sulayman narrated to us; Ibn Wahb narrated to me; 'Umar, that is Ibn Muhammad, narrated to me that Salim narrated to him, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar who said: "I never heard 'Umar say about anything: 'I think it is such,' except that it turned out as he thought. While 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was sitting, a handsome man passed by him, and he said: 'My assumption has been wrong, or this man is upon his religion in the Jahiliyyah, or he was their soothsayer. Bring the man to me.' So he was summoned and brought to him, and he said to him that. The man said: 'I have not seen a day like today, when a Muslim man is judged so.' He said: 'I urge you, by oath, to tell me.' He said: 'I was their soothsayer in the Jahiliyyah.' He said: 'What is the most amazing thing your jinn-wife brought you?' He said: 'One day while I was in the market, she came to me, and I recognised fear in her, and she said:

'Have you not seen the jinn and their despair,
and their giving up after their reversal,
and their pursuit of the riding camels and their saddle-cloths?'

'Umar said: 'She spoke the truth. While I was sleeping near their idols, a man came with a calf and slaughtered it, and a shouter shouted at him, a shout I had never heard louder than it, saying: "O Jalih, a successful affair, a man eloquent says: 'There is no god but Allah.'" The people leapt up, and I said: "I will not leave until I know what lies behind this." Then he called again: "O Jalih, a successful affair, a man eloquent says: 'There is no god but Allah.'" So I got up, and not long after it was said: "This is a Prophet."'"

This is the wording of al-Bukhari. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3866).]] Al-Bayhaqi related it from the hadith of Ibn Wahb, with similar wording, then said: "The apparent meaning of this report suggests that 'Umar himself heard the shouter crying out from the calf that was slaughtered, and likewise it is explicit in a weak report from 'Umar concerning his Islam, but all the other reports indicate that this soothsayer is the one who related that from his seeing and hearing, and Allah knows best." [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (2/245).]]

What al-Bayhaqi said is the most plausible. This man is Sawad ibn Qarib, and I have mentioned this in detail in the biography of 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, so whoever wants it should take it from there, and to Allah belongs all praise [and grace]. [[Addition from A.]]

Al-Bayhaqi said: "The hadith of Sawad ibn Qarib, and it may be that this is the soothsayer whose name was not mentioned in the authentic hadith."

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Habib al-Mufassir informed us, from the original of his hearing; Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Saffar al-Asbahani informed us, by reading to him: Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Musa al-Hammar al-Kufi narrated to us in Kufa; Ziyad ibn Yazid ibn Badawayh Abu Bakr al-Qasri narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Nawwas al-Kufi narrated to us; Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from T.]] who said: "While 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was delivering a sermon to the people from the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: 'O people, is Sawad ibn Qarib among you?' No one answered him that year. When the following year came, he said: 'O people, is Sawad ibn Qarib among you?' I said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, who is Sawad ibn Qarib?' 'Umar said to him: 'Sawad ibn Qarib's beginning of Islam was something amazing.' While we were in that state, Sawad ibn Qarib appeared, and 'Umar said to him: 'O Sawad, tell us about the beginning of your Islam, how was it?' Sawad said: 'I was staying in India, and I had a jinn companion. One night while I was sleeping, he came to me in that dream and said: "Arise, understand and reflect, if you are able to reflect, a messenger has been sent from Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib." Then he began to recite:

'I am amazed at the jinn and their vile ones, and their binding of camels with their saddle-cloths,
they fly towards Makkah seeking guidance; the believers among the jinn are not like their wicked ones.
So rise up towards the elite of Hashim, and wipe your eyes towards its head.'

He said: Then he woke me and frightened me, and said: 'O Sawad ibn Qarib, Allah has sent a Prophet, so rise towards him and you will be guided and rightly guided.' When it was the second night, he came to me, woke me, then began to recite similarly:

'I am amazed at the jinn and their pursuit, and their binding of camels with their saddles,
they fly towards Makkah seeking guidance; their leader is not like their tail.
So rise up towards the elite of Hashim, and wipe your eyes towards its fang.'

When it was the third night, he came to me, woke me, then said:

'I am amazed at the jinn and their knowledge of them, and their binding of camels with their pack-saddles,
they fly towards Makkah seeking guidance; those of evil are not like their righteous.
So rise up towards the elite of Hashim; the believers among the jinn are not like their disbelievers.'"

He said: When I heard it repeated night after night, the love of Islam entered my heart, by the will of Allah, from the matter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: I set off to my saddlebag, fastened it onto my riding camel, and had not yet untied one knot or tied another when I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He was in Al-Madinah, meaning Makkah, and the people around him were crowded like the mane of a horse. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw me, he said: "Welcome, O Sawad ibn Qarib. We already know what brought you." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have composed a poem, so let me recite it to you." Sawad said: I said:

*A visitor came to me after the first part of the night and sleep, and what I have experienced of him has never been a lie.*

*Three nights, his words each night: "A messenger has come to you from Luayy ibn Ghalib."*

*So I hitched up my izar above my shin and I was carried by a strong, swift she-camel among the open plains.*

*I bear witness that Allah, there is nothing besides Him, and that you are trusted over every unseen matter.*

*And that you are the nearest of the messengers in intercession to Allah, O son of the most noble and the purest.*

*So command us with what has come to you, O best of messengers, even if what came is grey-haired in its locks.*

*And be my intercessor on a day when no one has intercession except you, one who is sufficient in place of Sawad ibn Qarib.*

He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed until his molar teeth showed, and he said to me: "You have succeeded, O Sawad." Then Umar said to him: "Does your visitor still come to you now?" He said: "Since I recited the Qur'an, he has not come to me, and the Book of Allah is a better replacement for the jinn." (Dala'il al-nubuwwah by al-Bayhaqi, 1/248.)

Then al-Bayhaqi narrated it through two other chains. Among what indicates their delegation to him (peace be upon him) after he migrated to Al-Madinah is the report narrated by the hafiz (memorizer of hadith) Abu Nu'aym in his book Dala'il al-nubuwwah, saying:

Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Abdah al-Misisi narrated to us: Abu Tawbah al-Rabi' ibn Nafi' narrated to us: Mu'awiyah ibn Sallam narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, that he heard Abu Sallam say: "Someone who was told by Amr ibn Ghaylan al-Thaqafi narrated to me, saying: I came to Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and said to him: 'I have been told that you were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the delegation of the jinn.' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Tell me how the matter was.' He said: 'The People of the Suffah each took a man to feed him, and I was left, and none of them took me. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by me and said: "Who is this?" I said: "I am Ibn Mas'ud." He said: "Did no one take you to feed you?" I said: "No." He said: "Come along, perhaps I will find something for you." So we went until he came to the room of Umm Salamah, and he left me and entered among his family. Then a young servant girl came out and said: "O Ibn Mas'ud, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has not found supper for you, so return to your resting place." So I returned to the mosque, gathered the pebbles of the mosque, used them as a pillow, and wrapped myself in my garment. I had not waited long when the girl came and said: "Answer the call of the Messenger of Allah." So I followed her, hoping for supper, until when I reached my place, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out with a palm-frond stalk in his hand, placed it against my chest and said: "Will you go with me wherever I go?" I said: "As Allah wills." He repeated it to me three times, and each time I said: "As Allah wills." So he set off and I set off with him until we came to the Baqi' al-Gharqad. He drew a line with his staff and said: "Sit within it, and do not leave until I come to you." Then he walked on while I watched him between the palm trees, until, when he was out of my sight, a black dust cloud rose. I became frightened and said: "I will go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for I think Hawazin have plotted against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to kill him, so I will run to the houses and seek help from the people." But I remembered that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had instructed me not to leave the place where I was. Then I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) striking them with his staff and saying: "Sit down!" So they sat down until the column of dawn was almost splitting, then they rose and left. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to me and said: "Did you sleep after me?" I said: "No. By Allah, I was terrified with the first fright, to the point that I thought of going to the houses to seek help from the people, until I heard you striking them with your staff. I had thought it was Hawazin who had plotted against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to kill him." He said: "Had you left this circle, I would not have been secure for you from some of them snatching you. Did you see anything of them?" I said: "I saw black men with white garments tucked up." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Those were the delegation of the jinn of Nasibin. They came to me and asked me for provisions and goods, so I provided them with every bone that is bare, or dung, or droppings." I said: "And what good does that do them?" He said: "They never find a bone without finding on it the meat that was on it on the day it was eaten, and no dung without finding in it the grain that was in it the day it was eaten. So let none of you purify himself with a bone or droppings."' (I have not found this in the printed Dala'il al-nubuwwah of Abu Nu'aym.)"

This is a very strange chain, but it contains an unnamed man who is not identified [and Allah knows best]. Abu Nu'aym also narrated, from the hadith of Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid: Numayr ibn Zayd al-Qanbar narrated to me: my father narrated to us: Qahafah ibn Rabi'ah narrated to us: al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led us in the dawn prayer in the mosque of Al-Madinah, and when he finished he said: "Which of you will follow me to the delegation of the jinn tonight?" The people remained silent three times. Then he passed by me, took my hand, and I began walking with him until all the mountains of Al-Madinah were hidden from us, and we reached an open land. Suddenly there were tall men like spears, their garments tucked up between their legs. When I saw them, a violent trembling overtook me. Then he mentioned something similar to the earlier hadith of Ibn Mas'ud. (I have not found this in the printed Dala'il al-nubuwwah of Abu Nu'aym.) This is a strange hadith, and Allah knows best.

Among what relates to the delegation of the jinn is what Abu Nu'aym, the hafiz, narrated: Abu Muhammad ibn Hayyan narrated to us: Abu al-Tayyib Ahmad ibn Rawh narrated to us: Ya'qub al-Dawraqi narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Bukayr al-Tamimi narrated to us: Husayn ibn Umar (in one manuscript, "Umayr") narrated to us, and Ubayd al-Muktib informed me, from Ibrahim, who said: A group of the companions of Abdullah (in one manuscript, "Ubaydullah") set out wishing to perform Hajj. When they were on part of the road, they came upon a snake crawling across the road, white, from which the scent of musk was exhaling. I said to my companions: "Go on, for I will not leave until I see what becomes of this snake." He said: It did not remain long before it died. So I went to a white cloth, wrapped it in it, moved it off the road, and buried it. Then I caught up with my companions at the evening meal. He said: By Allah, we were sitting when four women came from the direction of the west. One of them said: "Which of you buried Amr?" We said: "Who is Amr?" She said: "Which of you buried the snake?" I said: "I did." She said: "By Allah, you buried a man who fasted often and prayed at night often, who commanded what Allah had revealed, and he believed in your Prophet and heard his description from the sky four hundred years before he was sent." The man said: We praised Allah, then completed our Hajj. Then I passed by Umar ibn al-Khattab in Al-Madinah and informed him of the matter of the snake. He said: "You have spoken truly. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'He believed in me four hundred years before I was sent.'" (Dala'il al-nubuwwah of Abu Nu'aym, p. 306.)

This is a very strange hadith, and Allah knows best.

Abu Nu'aym said: al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from al-Sha'bi, from a man of Thaqif, something similar. Abdullah ibn Ahmad and al-Zahrani narrated from Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal, the one who descended and buried that snake among the Companions, and that they said: "Indeed, he is the last of the nine who died among those who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) listening to the Qur'an." (I have not found this in the printed Dala'il al-nubuwwah of Abu Nu'aym.)

Abu Nu'aym also narrated, from the hadith of al-Layth ibn Sa'd, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Salamah al-Majishun, from his paternal uncle, from Mu'adh ibn Ubaydullah (in other manuscripts, "Abdullah") ibn Ma'mar, who said: I was sitting with Uthman ibn Affan when a man came and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, I was in a desert wasteland," and he mentioned that he saw two serpents (in other manuscripts, "two whirlwinds") fighting until one of them killed the other. He said: I went to the battlefield and found many dead snakes, and from some of them came the scent of musk. I began smelling them one by one until I found that scent from a thin, yellow snake. I wrapped it in my turban and buried it. As I was walking, a caller called to me (in one manuscript, "this is a jinn"): "O Abdullah, you have been guided! These are two groups of the jinn, the sons of Ash'iban and the sons of Uqaysh, who met, and what you saw of the dead occurred. The one you buried was martyred, and he was among those who heard the revelation from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He said: Uthman said to that man: "If you are truthful, then you have seen a wonder, and if you are lying, then your lie is upon you." (Dala'il al-nubuwwah of Abu Nu'aym, p. 305.)

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And [mention] when We turned toward you a group of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an﴾, that is, a company of the jinn. ﴿When they attended it, they said, "Be silent."﴾

That is: listen. And this was courtesy from them.

Al-Hafiz al-Bayhaqi said: Al-Imam Abu al-Tayyib Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman informed us: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Daqqaq informed us: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Bushanji narrated to us: Hisham ibn Ammar al-Dimashqi narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited Surah "al-Rahman" until he finished it, then said: "What is wrong with me that I see you silent? The jinn were better in response than you. Every time I recited to them this verse: ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ they said: 'Nor of any of Your blessings, our Lord, do we deny. So to You is the praise.'"

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Tafsir, from Abu Muslim Abd al-Rahman ibn Waqid, from al-Walid ibn Muslim with the same chain. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to his companions, recited to them Surah al-Rahman, and mentioned it. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib (strange); we do not know it except from the hadith of al-Walid, from Zuhayr," so he said. Al-Bayhaqi also narrated it from the hadith of Marwan ibn Muhammad al-Tatari, from Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, with a similar wording. (Dala'il al-nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi, 1/232, and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3291.)

* *

And His saying: ﴿When it was completed﴾, that is, finished, like His saying: ﴿And when the prayer is concluded﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 10], ﴿So He completed them as seven heavens in two days﴾ [Fussilat: 12], and ﴿And when you have completed your rites﴾ [al-Baqarah: 200]. ﴿They returned to their people as warners﴾, that is, they went back to their people and warned them of what they had heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, like His saying: ﴿So that they may gain understanding of the religion and warn their people when they return to them, that they may beware﴾ [al-Tawbah: 122].

This verse has been used as evidence that there were warners among the jinn, but that there were no messengers among them. There is no doubt that Allah did not send a messenger from among the jinn, as He says: ﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns﴾ [Yusuf: 109], and He says: ﴿And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets﴾ [al-Furqan: 20]. And He said about Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil): ﴿And We placed in his descendants prophethood and the Book﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 27].

So every prophet Allah sent after Abraham was from his descendants and progeny. As for His saying in [Surah] [[Addition from manuscript T.]] al-An'am: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ [al-An'am: 130], the meaning is the two kinds collectively, so it applies to one of them, which is mankind, like His saying: ﴿From both of them emerge the pearl and the coral﴾ [al-Rahman: 22], meaning from one of them.

Then He explained the warning of the jinn to their people, saying as He reports about them: ﴿They said, "O our people, indeed we have heard a Book revealed after Moses [confirming what came before it, guiding to the truth]"﴾ [[Addition from manuscript A.]], and they did not mention Jesus, because the Gospel was revealed to Jesus, peace be upon him, and it contains admonitions, softening of hearts, and a little of what is lawful and unlawful. It is in reality a complement to the law of the Torah, and the foundation is the Torah. For this reason they said: "revealed after Moses." Waraqah ibn Nawfal said the same when the Prophet ﷺ told him the story of Gabriel [peace be upon him] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] coming to him for the first time. He said: "Bakh bakh! This is the namus (the angel of revelation) that used to come to Moses. Would that I were young in it!"

﴿Confirming what came before it﴾, that is, of the Books sent down before it to the prophets. Their saying ﴿guiding to the truth﴾ means in belief and in reports, and ﴿to a straight path﴾ means in deeds. The Qur'an contains two kinds: information and command. Its information is true and its commands are just, as He said: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice﴾ [al-An'am: 115], and He said: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth﴾ [al-Tawbah: 33]. Guidance is beneficial knowledge, and the religion of truth is righteous action. Likewise the jinn said: ﴿guiding to the truth﴾ in matters of belief, and ﴿to a straight path﴾, that is, in practical matters.

﴿O our people, respond to the caller of Allah﴾. In this is an indication that Allah sent Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, to both the two weighty creations (al-thaqalayn), mankind and the jinn, when he called them to Allah, and he recited to them the surah which contains the address to both groups, their obligations, their promise and their warning, and that is Surah al-Rahman. For this reason they said: ﴿Respond to the caller of Allah and believe in him﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿He will forgive you of your sins﴾. It has been said that "min" here is extra (zā'idah), but this is questionable, since its addition in affirmative statements is rare. It has also been said that it retains its original function, of partitioning (lil-tab'id). ﴿And will protect you from a painful punishment﴾, that is, He will shield you from His painful punishment.

Scholars who held that believing jinn do not enter Paradise have used this verse as evidence, saying that the reward of their righteous ones is only to be spared the punishment of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. For this reason they said this in this context, which is a context of boasting and emphasis. If they had a reward for faith greater than this, they would surely have mentioned it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, saying: I was told on the authority of Jarir, from Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The believing jinn will not enter Paradise, because they are from the offspring of Iblis, and the offspring of Iblis will not enter Paradise."

The truth is that their believers, like the believers among mankind, will enter Paradise, as is the view of a group of the early generations (al-salaf). Some of them have used as evidence His saying: ﴿Neither man nor jinn has touched them before them﴾ [al-Rahman: 74], but this argument is questionable. Better than it is His saying: ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens. So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [al-Rahman: 46–47]. Allah has bestowed favor upon both the two weighty creations by making the reward of their righteous ones Paradise. The jinn responded to this verse with a verbal expression of gratitude more eloquent than mankind's, saying: "Nor of Your blessings, our Lord, do we deny anything. To You be praise." Allah would not bestow favor upon them with a reward that they would not receive. Also, if He repays their disbelievers with the Fire, which is a station of justice, then repaying their believers with Paradise, which is a station of grace, is all the more fitting and proper. Another proof of this is the generality of His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have the Gardens of Paradise as lodging﴾ [al-Kahf: 107], and similar verses. I have written a separate treatise on this question, and all praise and grace belong to Allah.

This Paradise continues to have room until Allah creates a new creation for it. Should He not then house in it whoever believed in Him and did righteous deeds? What they mentioned here as the reward for faith, namely the expiation of sins and protection from the painful punishment, necessarily implies entry into Paradise, because in the Hereafter there is only Paradise or the Fire. Whoever is spared the Fire enters Paradise without doubt. We have no explicit or apparent text from the Lawgiver stating that believing jinn will not enter Paradise even if they are spared the Fire. If such a text were authentic, we would adopt it, and Allah knows best.

And this is Noah, peace be upon him, saying to his people: ﴿He will forgive you of your sins and delay you until a specified term﴾ [Nuh: 4]. [[Variant from manuscripts T and A: "wa-yujirakum", which is an error.]] There is no disagreement that the believers among his people are in Paradise, and so are these.

Strange views have been reported about them. From 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz: they will not enter the central part of Paradise (bukhbuhat al-jannah), but will be in its outskirts (rabad), around it and in its edges. Some people claimed that in Paradise they will see the children of Adam while the children of Adam will not see them, the reverse of their situation in this worldly abode. Some people said: they do not eat or drink in Paradise, but are inspired with glorifying, praising and sanctifying God instead of food and drink, like the angels, because they are of the same kind as them. All these views are questionable, and there is no proof for them.

Then He said, reporting about them: ﴿And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah will not escape [Him] on earth﴾, that is, rather, the power of Allah encompasses him and surrounds him. ﴿And he will have no protectors other than Him﴾, that is, no one will shield them from Him. ﴿Those are in manifest error﴾. This is a station of threat and warning. They called their people both with encouragement and with warning, and for this reason many of them responded, and they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in delegations (wufud), delegation after delegation, as has been explained earlier.
